Error Mapping — thrown type -> HTTP response

Mermaid source 
%% Error Mapping — thrown type -> HTTP response
%% Owner: shared.GlobalExceptionHandler  (@RestControllerAdvice)
%% The diagram form of the "Error mapping" table in ../traceability.md.
%% ---
%% HOW TO READ THIS DIAGRAM
%%   SEVEN INDEPENDENT TRACKS, each running left to right on its own row:
%%     what raises it   ->   the exception type   ->   what the caller receives
%%   No track ever touches another, so a status code can be traced back to its
%%   trigger by reading one row straight across.
%% ---
%% WHY THE HANDLER LIVES IN shared
%%   Four modules throw; one class decides the status. If the handler lived in
%%   any one module, that module would own the HTTP translation of the other
%%   three — so it lives in shared, together with the four exception types, and
%%   depends on nothing. This is the ONE place in the system where an exception
%%   type meets a status code. No entity, service or listener mentions a status.

%%{init: {"flowchart": {"rankSpacing": 70, "nodeSpacing": 18, "curve": "linear"}}}%%
flowchart LR

  %% Column headers. No container boxes anywhere in this diagram: a subgraph
  %% laid out inside an LR graph puts its children side by side, which turned
  %% the seven tracks into three horizontal rows and re-created the arrow tangle
  %% this view exists to avoid. Three plain header nodes, one invisible chain.
  H1["<b>what raises it</b>"]
  H2["<b>the exception</b>"]
  H3["<b>what the caller receives</b>"]
  H1 ~~~ H2 ~~~ H3

  T1["@Valid on a request DTO<br/>the controller, BEFORE any service runs"]
  T2["a referenced aggregate or relationship<br/>does not exist<br/>a service, or a cross-module exists() returning false"]
  T3["a uniqueness rule is violated<br/>a service"]
  T4["a relationship rule is violated<br/>Book.assignTo()"]
  T5["a concurrent write wins the race<br/>a PostgreSQL UNIQUE or PRIMARY KEY constraint"]
  T7["a synchronous @EventListener fails<br/>during delete-student / delete-course"]
  T6["a bug<br/>anything unmapped"]

  E1["MethodArgumentNotValidException<br/>(Spring)"]
  E2["ResourceNotFoundException<br/>«shared»"]
  E3["DuplicateResourceException<br/>«shared»"]
  E4["InvalidRelationshipException<br/>«shared»"]
  E5["DataIntegrityViolationException<br/>(Spring Data)"]
  E7["whatever the listener threw<br/>propagates to the publisher"]
  E6["Exception"]

  R1["<b>400</b> ValidationErrorResponse<br/>fieldErrors[ field, message ]"]
  R2["<b>404</b> ErrorResponse<br/>STUDENT_NOT_FOUND · BOOK_NOT_FOUND<br/>COURSE_NOT_FOUND · ENROLLMENT_NOT_FOUND<br/>OWNERSHIP_NOT_FOUND · BOOK_NOT_ASSIGNED"]
  R3["<b>409</b> ErrorResponse<br/>STUDENT_CODE_EXISTS · EMAIL_EXISTS<br/>ISBN_EXISTS · COURSE_CODE_EXISTS<br/>ALREADY_ENROLLED"]
  R4["<b>409</b> ErrorResponse<br/>BOOK_ALREADY_ASSIGNED"]
  R5["<b>409</b> ErrorResponse<br/>the same code as the check that lost the race"]
  R7["<b>the listener's own status</b><br/>and the WHOLE transaction rolls back:<br/>the parent row is NOT deleted"]
  R6["<b>500</b> ErrorResponse<br/>INTERNAL_ERROR — message NOT echoed"]

  T1 --> E1 --> R1
  T2 --> E2 --> R2
  T3 --> E3 --> R3
  T4 --> E4 --> R4
  T5 --> E5 --> R5
  T7 --> E7 --> R7
  T6 --> E6 --> R6

%% =============================================================================
%% Rules this mapping asserts
%% =============================================================================
%% 1. A business rule collision is a 4xx. It is NEVER a 500. Track 5 exists for
%%    exactly this: the DB constraint firing under concurrency must land on the
%%    same status as the in-service check it duplicates.
%% ---
%% 2. TRACK 7 IS THE ONE THIS ARCHITECTURE ADDS, and it is not a new status —
%%    it is a guarantee about what happens to the transaction. The listeners in
%%    delete-student.mmd and delete-course.mmd are plain @EventListener calls
%%    running INSIDE the publisher's transaction, on the publisher's thread. So
%%    an exception thrown in a listener:
%%      - propagates straight back out of publishEvent()
%%      - is handled by GlobalExceptionHandler like any other, by its own type
%%      - rolls the ENTIRE operation back — the student or course is still there
%%    It does NOT become a 500, and it does NOT leave a half-cleaned parent.
%%    Had the listeners been @ApplicationModuleListener (async, after commit,
%%    own transaction), a failure there would be invisible to the caller, who
%%    would already have received 204 — that difference is the whole reason for
%%    the choice. See the footer of ../sequences/delete-student.mmd.
%% ---
%% 3. Track 6 should be unreachable in normal operation. Every reachable failure
%%    in ../traceability.md has a mapped exception. If a 500 appears in a log, a
%%    row is missing from this diagram — add it, do not widen track 6.
%% ---
%% 4. The exception carries the CODE; the handler chooses the STATUS. That split
%%    is what lets two different causes share 404 (BOOK_NOT_FOUND vs
%%    BOOK_NOT_ASSIGNED on UC23) and stay distinguishable to a client.
%% ---
%% 5. Bean validation runs before the service, so a 400 and a 409 can never be
%%    raised by the same request: a malformed payload never reaches a
%%    uniqueness check.
%% ---
%% 6. NO MODULE MENTIONS A STATUS CODE. A service throws
%%    ResourceNotFoundException("STUDENT_NOT_FOUND", ...); that 404 lives here
%%    and nowhere else. A cross-module exists() returns a boolean and throws
%%    nothing — the CALLING module decides that false is an error.
%% ---
%% =============================================================================
%% Where each code is raised
%% =============================================================================
%%   STUDENT_NOT_FOUND      ops 3,4,5,16,17,18,20,21,22   (../traceability.md)
%%   BOOK_NOT_FOUND         ops 8,9,10,16,17,19
%%   COURSE_NOT_FOUND       ops 13,14,15,20,21,23
%%   ENROLLMENT_NOT_FOUND   op 21                          unenroll.mmd
%%   OWNERSHIP_NOT_FOUND    op 17                          unassign-book.mmd
%%   BOOK_NOT_ASSIGNED      op 19                          get-book-owner.mmd
%%   STUDENT_CODE_EXISTS    ops 1,4                        create/update-student
%%   EMAIL_EXISTS           ops 1,4
%%   ISBN_EXISTS            ops 6,9
%%   COURSE_CODE_EXISTS     ops 11,14
%%   ALREADY_ENROLLED       op 20                          enroll.mmd
%%   BOOK_ALREADY_ASSIGNED  op 16                          assign-book.mmd
%% ---
%% =============================================================================
%% Not yet true in the code
%% =============================================================================
%% Track 1 requires spring-boot-starter-validation, which management/pom.xml
%% does not declare today. Without it @Valid is inert and every 400 in this
%% diagram silently becomes a 500 further down. See ../traceability.md,
%% "Implementation gaps", item 2.
%% ---
%% Track 5 requires the UNIQUE and PRIMARY KEY constraints to exist, and no
%% migration creates them yet — item 3 of the same list.

%% Class Diagram — Domain Model
%% org.phuchoang2005.management — four aggregates, one per application module.
%% ---
%% Reading rules:
%%   solid *--   composition INSIDE one aggregate: a value object owned by the
%%               entity that holds it. Never crosses a module boundary.
%%   dashed ..>  reference to ANOTHER aggregate, BY IDENTITY ONLY, and therefore
%%               also a cross-module dependency. Every dashed arrow here is one
%%               of the three solid edges in ../modules/module-map.mmd.
%% No aggregation and no composition crosses an aggregate boundary. There is no
%% @ManyToOne and no @ManyToMany in this system.
%% ---
%% WHAT IS NOT HERE, AND WHERE IT WENT
%%   - controllers, DTOs, error envelopes      -> ../modules/module-structure.mmd
%%   - which module may import which           -> ../modules/module-map.mmd
%%   - exception -> HTTP status                -> ../architecture/error-mapping.mmd
%%   - OwnershipPolicy / EnrollmentPolicy      -> deleted; see the footer

classDiagram
  direction LR

  %% ===========================================================================
  %% Module: student
  %% ===========================================================================

  class Student {
    <<Aggregate>>
    -Long id
    -StudentCode studentCode
    -String firstName
    -String lastName
    -Email email
    -LocalDate dateOfBirth
    -Instant createdAt
    -Instant updatedAt
    +StudentId id()
    +rename(String first, String last)
    +changeEmail(Email email)
  }

  class StudentRepository {
    <<JpaRepository~Student, Long~>>
    +Optional~Student~ findById(Long)
    +boolean existsById(Long)
    +boolean existsByStudentCode(StudentCode)
    +boolean existsByEmail(Email)
    +boolean existsByStudentCodeAndIdNot(StudentCode, Long)
    +boolean existsByEmailAndIdNot(Email, Long)
    +Page~Student~ search(String query, Pageable)
    +List~Student~ findAllByIdIn(List~Long~)
    +Student save(Student)
    +void deleteById(Long)
  }

  class StudentService {
    <<Service>>
    +StudentResponse createStudent(StudentCreateRequest)
    +StudentResponse getStudent(StudentId)
    +Page~StudentResponse~ listStudents(String, Pageable)
    +StudentResponse updateStudent(StudentId, StudentUpdateRequest)
    +void deleteStudent(StudentId)
    +boolean exists(StudentId)
    +Optional~StudentSummaryResponse~ summaryOf(StudentId)
    +List~StudentSummaryResponse~ summariesOf(List~StudentId~)
  }

  class StudentDeleted {
    <<DomainEvent>>
    +StudentId studentId
  }

  %% ===========================================================================
  %% Module: course
  %% ===========================================================================

  class Course {
    <<Aggregate>>
    -Long id
    -CourseCode courseCode
    -String name
    -String description
    -Integer credits
    -Instant createdAt
    -Instant updatedAt
    +CourseId id()
    +changeCredits(Integer credits)
  }

  class CourseRepository {
    <<JpaRepository~Course, Long~>>
    +Optional~Course~ findById(Long)
    +boolean existsById(Long)
    +boolean existsByCourseCode(CourseCode)
    +boolean existsByCourseCodeAndIdNot(CourseCode, Long)
    +Page~Course~ search(String query, Pageable)
    +List~Course~ findAllByIdIn(List~Long~)
    +Course save(Course)
    +void deleteById(Long)
  }

  class CourseService {
    <<Service>>
    +CourseResponse createCourse(CourseCreateRequest)
    +CourseResponse getCourse(CourseId)
    +Page~CourseResponse~ listCourses(String, Pageable)
    +CourseResponse updateCourse(CourseId, CourseUpdateRequest)
    +void deleteCourse(CourseId)
    +boolean exists(CourseId)
    +List~CourseResponse~ responsesOf(List~CourseId~)
  }

  class CourseDeleted {
    <<DomainEvent>>
    +CourseId courseId
  }

  %% ===========================================================================
  %% Module: book
  %% ===========================================================================

  class Book {
    <<Aggregate>>
    -Long id
    -ISBN isbn
    -String title
    -String author
    -LocalDate publishedDate
    -StudentId ownerId
    -Instant createdAt
    -Instant updatedAt
    +BookId id()
    +boolean isOwned()
    +boolean isOwnedBy(StudentId)
    +assignTo(StudentId newOwner)
    +release()
  }

  class BookRepository {
    <<JpaRepository~Book, Long~>>
    +Optional~Book~ findById(Long)
    +boolean existsByIsbn(ISBN)
    +boolean existsByIsbnAndIdNot(ISBN, Long)
    +List~Book~ findByOwnerId(StudentId)
    +Page~Book~ search(String query, Pageable)
    +Book save(Book)
    +void deleteById(Long)
  }

  class BookService {
    <<Service>>
    +BookResponse createBook(BookCreateRequest)
    +BookResponse getBook(BookId)
    +Page~BookResponse~ listBooks(String, Pageable)
    +BookResponse updateBook(BookId, BookUpdateRequest)
    +void deleteBook(BookId)
  }

  class BookOwnershipService {
    <<Service>>
    +BookResponse assignBook(StudentId, BookId)
    +void unassignBook(StudentId, BookId)
    +List~BookResponse~ listBooksOf(StudentId)
    +StudentSummaryResponse findOwner(BookId)
  }

  class BookStudentDeletedListener {
    <<EventListener>>
    +void on(StudentDeleted event)
  }

  %% ===========================================================================
  %% Module: enrollment
  %% ===========================================================================

  class Enrollment {
    <<Aggregate>>
    -EnrollmentId id
    -Instant enrolledAt
    +StudentId studentId()
    +CourseId courseId()
    +static Enrollment open(StudentId, CourseId)
  }

  class EnrollmentId {
    <<Embeddable>>
    +Long studentId
    +Long courseId
  }

  class EnrollmentRepository {
    <<JpaRepository~Enrollment, EnrollmentId~>>
    +boolean existsById(EnrollmentId)
    +Optional~Enrollment~ findById(EnrollmentId)
    +List~Enrollment~ findByIdStudentId(Long)
    +List~Enrollment~ findByIdCourseId(Long)
    +Enrollment save(Enrollment)
    +void deleteById(EnrollmentId)
    +void deleteByIdStudentId(Long)
    +void deleteByIdCourseId(Long)
  }

  class EnrollmentService {
    <<Service>>
    +EnrollmentResponse enroll(StudentId, CourseId)
    +void unenroll(StudentId, CourseId)
    +List~CourseResponse~ coursesOf(StudentId)
    +List~StudentSummaryResponse~ studentsIn(CourseId)
  }

  class EnrollmentCleanupListener {
    <<EventListener>>
    +void on(StudentDeleted event)
    +void on(CourseDeleted event)
  }

  %% ===========================================================================
  %% Value objects — identity
  %% ===========================================================================

  class StudentId {
    <<ValueObject>>
    +Long value
  }
  class CourseId {
    <<ValueObject>>
    +Long value
  }
  class BookId {
    <<ValueObject>>
    +Long value
  }

  %% ===========================================================================
  %% Value objects — business
  %% ===========================================================================

  class StudentCode {
    <<ValueObject>>
    +String value
    +static StudentCode of(String raw)
  }
  class CourseCode {
    <<ValueObject>>
    +String value
    +static CourseCode of(String raw)
  }
  class ISBN {
    <<ValueObject>>
    +String value
    +static ISBN of(String raw)
  }
  class Email {
    <<ValueObject>>
    +String value
    +static Email of(String raw)
  }

  %% ===========================================================================
  %% Module: shared — the exception hierarchy
  %% ===========================================================================

  class DomainException {
    <<abstract>>
    +String code
    +String message
  }
  class ResourceNotFoundException {
    <<DomainException>>
  }
  class DuplicateResourceException {
    <<DomainException>>
  }
  class InvalidRelationshipException {
    <<DomainException>>
  }

  DomainException <|-- ResourceNotFoundException
  DomainException <|-- DuplicateResourceException
  DomainException <|-- InvalidRelationshipException

  %% ===========================================================================
  %% Aggregate -> value object composition (INSIDE the aggregate — allowed)
  %% ===========================================================================

  Student *-- StudentCode
  Student *-- Email
  Course *-- CourseCode
  Book *-- ISBN
  Enrollment *-- EnrollmentId

  %% ===========================================================================
  %% Cross-aggregate references — IDENTITY ONLY, and therefore cross-module
  %% ===========================================================================

  Book ..> StudentId : ownerId (nullable)
  Enrollment ..> StudentId : studentId()
  Enrollment ..> CourseId : courseId()

  %% ===========================================================================
  %% Wiring inside a module
  %% ===========================================================================

  StudentService ..> StudentRepository
  StudentService ..> Student
  StudentService ..> StudentDeleted : publishes
  CourseService ..> CourseRepository
  CourseService ..> Course
  CourseService ..> CourseDeleted : publishes
  BookService ..> BookRepository
  BookService ..> Book
  BookOwnershipService ..> BookRepository
  BookOwnershipService ..> Book
  EnrollmentService ..> EnrollmentRepository
  EnrollmentService ..> Enrollment

  %% ===========================================================================
  %% Cross-module calls and event subscriptions
  %% ===========================================================================

  BookOwnershipService ..> StudentService : exists / summaryOf
  EnrollmentService ..> StudentService : exists / summariesOf
  EnrollmentService ..> CourseService : exists / responsesOf
  BookStudentDeletedListener ..> StudentDeleted : consumes
  BookStudentDeletedListener ..> BookRepository
  EnrollmentCleanupListener ..> StudentDeleted : consumes
  EnrollmentCleanupListener ..> CourseDeleted : consumes
  EnrollmentCleanupListener ..> EnrollmentRepository

  %% ===========================================================================
  %% Invariants
  %% ===========================================================================

  note for StudentCode "format ^STU[0-9]{3,}$ — unique across Students (409 on duplicate).\nPersisted by StudentCodeConverter : AttributeConverter~StudentCode, String~\nto students.student_code VARCHAR."
  note for Email "RFC-5322 shape — unique across Students (409 on duplicate).\nPersisted by EmailConverter to students.email VARCHAR."
  note for CourseCode "format ^[A-Z]{2,4}[0-9]{3}$ — unique across Courses (409 on duplicate).\nPersisted by CourseCodeConverter to courses.course_code VARCHAR."
  note for ISBN "10 or 13 digits — unique across Books (409 on duplicate).\nPersisted by IsbnConverter to books.isbn VARCHAR."
  note for StudentId "Published API of the student module: book and enrollment both store it.\nAs an ENTITY ID it is NOT the mapped field — Student keeps @Id @GeneratedValue\nLong id and exposes id() : StudentId. @EmbeddedId with @GeneratedValue does not\nwork in Hibernate; do not attempt it.\nAs Book.ownerId it IS mapped, by StudentIdConverter : AttributeConverter~StudentId, Long~\nto books.student_id BIGINT NULL."
  note for Course "credits must be positive (@Positive on the request DTO,\nCHECK (credits > 0) in the schema, guarded again in changeCredits)."
  note for StudentRepository "existsBy*(x) answers create-time uniqueness.\nexistsBy*AndIdNot(x, id) answers UPDATE-time uniqueness — the\nsame check EXCLUDING the row being updated. Using the first form\non a PUT makes a student conflict with their own studentCode.\nSee ../sequences/update-student.mmd."
  note for Enrollment "identity IS (studentId, courseId), mapped as @EmbeddedId EnrollmentId\nholding RAW Longs — nesting converted value objects inside an @EmbeddedId is\nwhere this design stops being worth it. studentId() and courseId() wrap on read.\nUniqueness of the pair is the no-duplicate-enrolment invariant, enforced by\nEnrollmentService and by the composite PRIMARY KEY on student_courses."
  note for Book "single-owner invariant, and it lives HERE rather than in a service because it\nreads only the book's own state:\n  assignTo(y) on a book owned by x != y throws InvalidRelationshipException (409)\n  assignTo(x) on a book already owned by x is idempotent\n  release() is idempotent"
  note for EnrollmentService "the duplicate-enrollment rule lives in the SERVICE, not on the entity,\nbecause it needs a repository lookup. An entity that holds a repository\nis not an entity. That asymmetry with Book is deliberate."
  note for Student "deleting a Student does NOT cascade to Books. StudentService publishes\nStudentDeleted BEFORE removing the row; the book module releases owned books\nand the enrollment module drops enrollments, synchronously, in the same\ntransaction. See ../sequences/delete-student.mmd."

%% =============================================================================
%% What this model dropped from the pure-DDD version, and why
%% =============================================================================
%% OwnershipPolicy «DomainService»
%%   assertAssignable(book, candidate) -> Book.assignTo(newOwner)
%%   assertOwnedBy(book, owner)        -> Book.isOwnedBy(owner) + a throw in
%%                                        BookOwnershipService
%%   Both only read the book's own state, so the aggregate can enforce them. The
%%   policy was a class whose entire body was an if and a throw.
%% ---
%% EnrollmentPolicy «DomainService»
%%   assertNotEnrolled / assertEnrolled -> EnrollmentService, which already holds
%%   the repository the check needs. Extracting a stateless class that takes the
%%   repository as a constructor argument adds a name, not a boundary.
%% ---
%% StudentRepository / CourseRepository / BookRepository / EnrollmentRepository
%% as hand-written DOMAIN INTERFACES with separate Spring Data implementations
%%   -> one JpaRepository each, in module/internal/. The split existed to keep
%%   the wrong code from depending on Spring Data. Module visibility now does
%%   that: no class outside book/ can name BookRepository at all.
%% ---
%% What was NOT dropped: all seven value objects, every invariant note above,
%% identity-only references, one transaction per use case, and the ubiquitous
%% language. Those are the parts of DDD that were paying for themselves.
%% ---
%% =============================================================================
%% OUT OF SCOPE for this diagram
%% =============================================================================
%% Controllers, request/response DTOs, PageMetadata and the error envelopes live
%% in each module's root package and are specified by ../../api-contract/.
%% They are absent here so the model stays readable; see
%% ../modules/module-structure.mmd for how a module fits together.
%% ---
%% Pageable / Page above are Spring Data types appearing in repository and
%% service signatures only; they never enter an aggregate.

%% Deployment Diagram — how the system actually runs TODAY (local development)
%% Sources of truth: docker-compose.yml, Makefile, .env.example,
%% management/pom.xml, management/src/main/resources/application.properties
%% ---
%% HOW TO READ THIS DIAGRAM
%%   Boxes are NODES (a machine, a VM, a container, a process). The one solid
%%   arrow is the only network hop in the system. Everything else is containment.
%%   If you are looking for the internal call graph, this is the wrong file —
%%   see ../modules/module-map.mmd.
%% ---
%% THE POINT OF THIS DIAGRAM, STATED ONCE
%%   There is exactly ONE deployable process and ONE database. The five
%%   application modules are PACKAGES INSIDE A SINGLE JVM, not services. They
%%   share one classloader, one connection pool, one transaction manager and one
%%   schema. Nothing in this system crosses a process boundary except JDBC.
%% ---
%%   That is what makes the whole design work: because a cross-module call is an
%%   ordinary method call and a domain event is an in-process, in-transaction
%%   dispatch, module boundaries cost nothing at runtime. A modulith buys the
%%   organisation of microservices at the price of a monolith — and the price of
%%   microservices is exactly the picture below, multiplied.

flowchart TB

  subgraph DEV["💻 Developer machine  —  macOS"]
    direction TB

    subgraph JVM["JVM process  —  java 21  —  ONE process, five modules"]
      direction TB
      APP["Spring Boot 4.1.0 application<br/>org.phuchoang2005.management<br/>modules: shared · student · course · book · enrollment<br/>spring-boot-starter-webmvc + data-jpa + validation<br/>spring-modulith-starter-core<br/>run: ./mvnw spring-boot:run"]
      HTTP["embedded Tomcat<br/>listens on :8080<br/>base path /api/v1"]
      TX["one transaction manager<br/>every use case, and every listener it triggers,<br/>runs in ONE transaction on ONE thread"]
    end

    subgraph COLIMA["Colima VM  —  container runtime  (make up / make down)"]
      direction TB
      subgraph COMPOSE["docker compose  —  docker-compose.yml"]
        direction TB
        PG["container: management-postgres<br/>image postgres:16-alpine<br/>restart: unless-stopped<br/>healthcheck: pg_isready every 5s"]
        VOL[("named volume: postgres_data<br/>/var/lib/postgresql/data<br/>survives 'make down' — destroyed by 'make clean'")]
      end
    end

    ENV["/.env  (git-ignored, copied from .env.example by 'make env')<br/>POSTGRES_DB · POSTGRES_USER · POSTGRES_PASSWORD · POSTGRES_PORT"]
  end

  CLIENT["🖥️ API client<br/>curl · Postman · the future front-end"]

  BUILD["🔧 build time only — no runtime component<br/>ModuleStructureTest: ApplicationModules.verify()<br/>Documenter: regenerates module diagrams + canvases<br/>./mvnw test — see ../../modulith-verification.md"]

  CLIENT -->|"HTTP  localhost:8080/api/v1/..."| HTTP
  HTTP --- APP
  APP --- TX
  APP ==>|"JDBC  jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5432/management<br/>the only network hop inside the system"| PG
  PG --- VOL
  ENV -.->|"docker compose reads it"| PG
  ENV -.->|"exported by the Makefile — the app reads the same<br/>names in application.properties"| APP
  BUILD -.->|"verifies the module structure of"| APP

  classDef app fill:#ffe,stroke:#333;
  classDef db fill:#efe,stroke:#333;
  classDef vol fill:#ddd,stroke:#333;
  classDef ext fill:#fde,stroke:#333;
  classDef cfg fill:#fafafa,stroke:#bbb,color:#555,stroke-dasharray:3 3;

  class APP,HTTP,TX app
  class PG db
  class VOL vol
  class CLIENT ext
  class ENV,BUILD cfg

  style DEV fill:#fdfdfd,stroke:#999
  style COLIMA fill:#f6faff,stroke:#3b4a9c
  style COMPOSE fill:#fbfdff,stroke:#88a,stroke-dasharray:4 3
  style JVM fill:#fffdf5,stroke:#c9a227

%% =============================================================================
%% Lifecycle — the commands, in order
%% =============================================================================
%%   make up      colima start; docker compose up -d   (creates .env if missing)
%%   ./mvnw spring-boot:run   from management/         (the app runs on the HOST,
%%                                                      not in a container)
%%   ./mvnw test              runs ModuleStructureTest first — it is the fastest
%%                            test in the suite and the one that fails when an
%%                            import crosses a boundary it should not
%%   make psql    psql shell inside the container
%%   make logs    tail postgres logs
%%   make down    docker compose down; colima stop      (data survives)
%%   make clean   docker compose down -v                (data destroyed)
%%   make reset   clean + up                            (fresh database)
%% ---
%% =============================================================================
%% Spring Modulith adds NOTHING to this picture at runtime
%% =============================================================================
%% spring-modulith-starter-core contributes @ApplicationModule (an annotation
%% read by tests and by Documenter) and the module model. It starts no server,
%% opens no port, creates no table and adds no thread.
%% ---
%% The one Modulith feature that WOULD change this diagram is the asynchronous
%% event stack: spring-modulith-starter-jpa creates an event_publication table
%% for the outbox, and @ApplicationModuleListener adds a task executor. This
%% project uses neither — its events are synchronous and in-transaction (rule M4
%% in ../modules/module-map.mmd). If that ever changes, this diagram gains a
%% table and a thread pool, and the "one transaction" note on the JVM node
%% becomes false.
%% ---
%% =============================================================================
%% Deliberately NOT in this picture, and why
%% =============================================================================
%% No app container.  The application runs on the host JVM against a
%%   containerised database. There is no Dockerfile for the app yet; a
%%   production topology would add one plus a compose service for it.
%% No second service.  The modules are not deployables and splitting one out is
%%   not a planned step. If it ever happened, the synchronous cross-module calls
%%   in ../traceability.md ("Cross-module inventory") become network calls and
%%   the synchronous events become an eventually-consistent saga — a different
%%   architecture, not a configuration change.
%% No security.  spring-boot-starter-security is commented out in pom.xml and
%%   the OpenAPI contract defines no security scheme, so :8080 is wide open.
%%   application.properties still carries dead spring.security.user.* values —
%%   ../traceability.md, "Implementation gaps", item 4.
%% No schema migration.  Nothing in this picture creates tables. There is no
%%   Flyway dependency and no spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto setting, so a fresh
%%   'make reset' leaves an EMPTY database that the app cannot write to. This is
%%   the first thing to fix before any of the sequence diagrams can run —
%%   ../traceability.md, "Implementation gaps", item 3.
%% No Swagger UI.  ../modules/module-structure.mmd lists an OpenApiConfig in the
%%   shared module, but springdoc is not a dependency yet. Until it is,
%%   ../../api-contract/openapi.yml is the only contract artefact and it is
%%   hand-maintained.
%% No Spring Modulith dependency at all, yet — item 1 of the same list. Every
%%   module boundary in this documentation set is currently a promise rather
%%   than a check.
%% ---
%% =============================================================================
%% What changes when this is deployed for real
%% =============================================================================
%% The application node moves into its own container next to postgres, the JDBC
%% URL's host becomes the compose service name instead of localhost, and the
%% .env values come from the platform's secret store rather than a file. The
%% shape of this diagram — one process, one database, one hop — does not change,
%% and neither does the module structure: it is a property of the source tree,
%% not of the topology.

modules/module-map.mmd

Module Map — Spring Modulith application modules

Mermaid source 
%% Module Map — Spring Modulith application modules
%% org.phuchoang2005.management — ONE Spring Boot application, FIVE application modules.
%% ---
%% This is the top-level architecture diagram. Everything else in this folder
%% elaborates one box or one arrow on it.
%% ---
%% WHAT AN "APPLICATION MODULE" IS HERE
%%   Every direct sub-package of org.phuchoang2005.management is an application
%%   module in the Spring Modulith sense. Types in the module's ROOT package are
%%   its published API; types in any SUB-package (internal/) are invisible to
%%   every other module. This is not a convention — it is checked by
%%   ApplicationModules.of(ManagementApplication.class).verify() running as a
%%   JUnit test. See ../../modulith-verification.md.
%% ---
%% HOW TO READ THIS DIAGRAM
%%   SOLID arrow  = a compile-time dependency, declared in @ApplicationModule
%%                  allowedDependencies. Reading it as "imports from".
%%   DASHED arrow = a domain event travelling the OPPOSITE way along an edge
%%                  that already exists. It is not a new dependency: the
%%                  listener lives in the DOWNSTREAM module and imports the
%%                  event type from the upstream one, which the solid arrow
%%                  already permits.
%% ---
%%   The solid graph is ACYCLIC and that is the whole point. Read it bottom-up:
%%   shared depends on nobody, student and course depend only on shared, book
%%   adds student, enrollment adds both. If you can draw a cycle on this
%%   picture, verify() fails and the build goes red.

flowchart TB

  subgraph APP["Spring Boot application  —  org.phuchoang2005.management"]
    direction TB

    subgraph L3["depends on two peers"]
      direction LR
      ENR["<b>enrollment</b><br/>Enrollment «Aggregate»<br/>EnrollmentService<br/>StudentCourseController<br/>—<br/>invariant: no duplicate<br/>(studentId, courseId)"]
    end

    subgraph L2["depends on one peer"]
      direction LR
      BOOK["<b>book</b><br/>Book «Aggregate»<br/>BookService · BookOwnershipService<br/>BookController · StudentBookController<br/>—<br/>invariant: a book has<br/>at most one owner"]
    end

    subgraph L1["depend on shared only"]
      direction LR
      STU["<b>student</b><br/>Student «Aggregate»<br/>StudentService<br/>StudentController<br/>—<br/>invariant: studentCode<br/>and email are unique"]
      CRS["<b>course</b><br/>Course «Aggregate»<br/>CourseService<br/>CourseController<br/>—<br/>invariant: courseCode unique,<br/>credits &gt; 0"]
    end

    SHR["<b>shared</b>  «open module»<br/>DomainException · ResourceNotFoundException<br/>DuplicateResourceException · InvalidRelationshipException<br/>GlobalExceptionHandler · ErrorResponse · ValidationErrorResponse<br/>PageMetadata · JpaAuditingConfig · OpenApiConfig<br/>—<br/>owns no table, no aggregate, no rule"]
  end

  %% ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  %% Solid edges — declared allowedDependencies
  %% ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  STU  ==> SHR
  CRS  ==> SHR
  BOOK ==> SHR
  ENR  ==> SHR

  BOOK ==>|"Book.ownerId : StudentId<br/>StudentService.exists()"| STU
  ENR  ==>|"Enrollment.studentId : StudentId<br/>StudentService.summariesOf()"| STU
  ENR  ==>|"Enrollment.courseId : CourseId<br/>CourseService.responsesOf()"| CRS

  %% ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  %% Dashed edges — domain events, travelling back up an existing solid edge
  %% ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  STU -.->|"StudentDeleted<br/>@EventListener releases owned books"| BOOK
  STU -.->|"StudentDeleted<br/>@EventListener drops enrollments"| ENR
  CRS -.->|"CourseDeleted<br/>@EventListener drops enrollments"| ENR

  classDef mod fill:#eef,stroke:#3b4a9c,stroke-width:2px,color:#111;
  classDef lib fill:#efe,stroke:#2d7a2d,stroke-width:2px,color:#111;
  classDef rel fill:#fff4e0,stroke:#b8860b,stroke-width:2px,color:#111;
  classDef shr fill:#fafafa,stroke:#888,stroke-dasharray:4 3,color:#333;
  classDef band fill:#fdfdfd,stroke:#ddd,color:#777;

  class STU,CRS mod
  class BOOK lib
  class ENR rel
  class SHR shr
  class L1,L2,L3 band
  style APP fill:#ffffff,stroke:#999

%% =============================================================================
%% The declaration this diagram is drawn from
%% =============================================================================
%%   student/package-info.java
%%     @ApplicationModule(allowedDependencies = {"shared"})
%%   course/package-info.java
%%     @ApplicationModule(allowedDependencies = {"shared"})
%%   book/package-info.java
%%     @ApplicationModule(allowedDependencies = {"shared", "student"})
%%   enrollment/package-info.java
%%     @ApplicationModule(allowedDependencies = {"shared", "student", "course"})
%%   shared/package-info.java
%%     @ApplicationModule(type = Type.OPEN)
%% ---
%% shared is OPEN so its sub-packages stay reachable and so it does not need to
%% declare anything about the modules that use it. An open module is exempt from
%% the internal/-is-hidden rule; that exemption is acceptable precisely because
%% shared holds no business rule. If a rule ever lands in shared, close it.
%% ---
%% =============================================================================
%% Rules this map asserts   (M1-M5 — the successors of R1-R4 in the pure-DDD version)
%% =============================================================================
%% M1. Aggregates reference each other BY IDENTITY, never by object reference.
%%     Book holds ownerId : StudentId, not a Student. Enrollment holds
%%     studentId : StudentId and courseId : CourseId, not the aggregates. There
%%     is no @ManyToOne and no @ManyToMany anywhere in this system.
%% ---
%% M2. A module publishes only what another module needs. Entities and
%%     repositories live in internal/ and are unreachable from outside. A module
%%     that needs data from another asks its SERVICE and receives a DTO or a
%%     value object — never an entity. This is enforced, not requested.
%% ---
%% M3. The solid dependency graph is acyclic, and stays that way because
%%     cross-module CLEANUP travels as an event along an edge that already
%%     exists, in the reverse direction. student never imports book; book
%%     imports student.StudentDeleted, which M-edge book==>student already
%%     allows.
%% ---
%% M4. Those events are SYNCHRONOUS and IN-TRANSACTION: plain @EventListener,
%%     published before the parent row is removed. One transaction, one
%%     rollback, correct FK ordering. NOT @ApplicationModuleListener, NOT
%%     @TransactionalEventListener — see the ordering note in
%%     ../sequences/delete-student.mmd, which is the reason.
%% ---
%% M5. shared is a leaf. It depends on no module and contains no business rule.
%%     Anything that knows what a Student IS does not belong there.
%% ---
%% =============================================================================
%% Why five modules and not two
%% =============================================================================
%% The pure-DDD version of these documents grouped the same four aggregates into
%% two modules, academic (Student, Course, Enrollment) and library (Book), and
%% enforced the split by review. Two things changed:
%%   - Modulith can only enforce boundaries it can see. Folding Enrollment into
%%     an academic module hides the most interesting boundary in the system —
%%     enrollment reaches into two peers — inside a package where nothing checks
%%     it.
%%   - One module per aggregate makes the module graph and the aggregate graph
%%     the same picture, so there is one fewer mapping to keep in your head.
%% ---
%% =============================================================================
%% Deferred, NOT current design
%% =============================================================================
%% Asynchronous events, @ApplicationModuleListener, the event_publication
%% registry (spring-modulith-starter-jpa) and eventual consistency are
%% deliberately out of scope. They buy resilience this system does not need and
%% cost an outbox table, a retry story, and an FK that must become
%% ON DELETE SET NULL. If these modules are ever split into separate
%% deployables, that is the moment to adopt them — not before.

Module Structure

modules/module-structure.mmd

Module Structure — what is inside one module, and what escapes it

Mermaid source 
%% Module Structure — what is inside one module, and what escapes it
%% org.phuchoang2005.management
%% ---
%% module-map.mmd draws the FIVE BOXES and the arrows between them. This file
%% opens the boxes.
%% ---
%% HOW TO READ THIS DIAGRAM
%%   TOP TO BOTTOM = VISIBILITY, and it is the only axis that matters.
%%     upper band  = the module ROOT package  -> PUBLISHED, importable by anyone
%%     lower band  = the module internal/ package -> HIDDEN, importable by nobody
%%   The dashed line between the two bands is the boundary Spring Modulith
%%   enforces. Every solid arrow that crosses a module boundary in this picture
%%   lands in an upper band. Not one lands in a lower band — that is the diagram
%%   equivalent of the verify() test passing.
%% ---
%%   LEFT TO RIGHT = MODULE. Four vertical slices, one per aggregate, each
%%   containing its own controller, service, DTOs, entity and repository. There
%%   is no api/ package, no application/ package, no infrastructure/ package.
%%   The layers still exist — they are just stacked INSIDE a slice instead of
%%   across the whole application.
%% ---
%%   Intra-module wiring is NOT drawn. A controller uses its own service, which
%%   uses its own repository and its own mapper; drawing 20 obvious arrows is
%%   what made the previous version of this diagram unreadable. Only arrows that
%%   CROSS A MODULE BOUNDARY appear, because those are the ones with rules.

%%{init: {"flowchart": {"rankSpacing": 55, "nodeSpacing": 24, "curve": "linear"}}}%%
flowchart TB

  %% ===========================================================================
  %% Band 1 — published API. Other modules may import these.
  %% ===========================================================================
  subgraph PUB["PUBLISHED  —  the module root package  —  importable by any module"]
    direction LR

    P_STU["<b>student/</b><br/>StudentController<br/>StudentService<br/>StudentId · StudentCode · Email «VO»<br/>StudentDeleted «Event»<br/>StudentCreateRequest · StudentUpdateRequest<br/>StudentResponse · StudentSummaryResponse"]
    P_CRS["<b>course/</b><br/>CourseController<br/>CourseService<br/>CourseId · CourseCode «VO»<br/>CourseDeleted «Event»<br/>CourseCreateRequest · CourseUpdateRequest<br/>CourseResponse"]
    P_BOK["<b>book/</b><br/>BookController · StudentBookController<br/>BookService · BookOwnershipService<br/>BookId · ISBN «VO»<br/>BookCreateRequest · BookUpdateRequest<br/>BookResponse"]
    P_ENR["<b>enrollment/</b><br/>StudentCourseController<br/>EnrollmentService<br/>EnrollmentResponse"]
  end

  %% ===========================================================================
  %% Band 2 — internal. NOTHING outside the slice may import these.
  %% ===========================================================================
  subgraph INT["INTERNAL  —  module/internal/  —  importable by NOBODY else"]
    direction LR

    I_STU["<b>student/internal/</b><br/>Student «Entity»<br/>StudentRepository<br/>StudentMapper<br/>StudentCodeConverter · EmailConverter"]
    I_CRS["<b>course/internal/</b><br/>Course «Entity»<br/>CourseRepository<br/>CourseMapper<br/>CourseCodeConverter"]
    I_BOK["<b>book/internal/</b><br/>Book «Entity»<br/>BookRepository<br/>BookMapper<br/>IsbnConverter · StudentIdConverter<br/>StudentDeletedListener"]
    I_ENR["<b>enrollment/internal/</b><br/>Enrollment «Entity» · EnrollmentId<br/>EnrollmentRepository<br/>StudentDeletedListener · CourseDeletedListener"]
  end

  %% ===========================================================================
  %% Band 3 — shared, open. Everything above may import it.
  %% ===========================================================================
  SHR["<b>shared/</b>  «open module»  —  no entity, no repository, no rule<br/>DomainException · ResourceNotFoundException · DuplicateResourceException · InvalidRelationshipException<br/>GlobalExceptionHandler «@RestControllerAdvice» · ErrorResponse · ValidationErrorResponse · PageMetadata<br/>JpaAuditingConfig · OpenApiConfig"]

  %% ===========================================================================
  %% Band 4 — the one database
  %% ===========================================================================
  DB[("PostgreSQL 16 — one schema<br/>students · books · courses · student_courses")]

  %% ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  %% Cross-module arrows. Every one lands in the PUBLISHED band.
  %% ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  P_BOK ==>|"exists(StudentId)"| P_STU
  P_ENR ==>|"exists · summariesOf"| P_STU
  P_ENR ==>|"exists · responsesOf"| P_CRS

  I_BOK -.->|"listens to student.StudentDeleted"| P_STU
  I_ENR -.->|"listens to StudentDeleted"| P_STU
  I_ENR -.->|"listens to CourseDeleted"| P_CRS

  %% ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  %% Persistence. Each module owns its own tables and reaches no other's.
  %% ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  I_STU --> DB
  I_CRS --> DB
  I_BOK --> DB
  I_ENR --> DB

  classDef pub fill:#eef,stroke:#3b4a9c,stroke-width:2px,color:#111;
  classDef int fill:#f7f7f7,stroke:#999,stroke-dasharray:4 3,color:#333;
  classDef shr fill:#fafafa,stroke:#888,color:#333;
  classDef db  fill:#ddd,stroke:#333,color:#111;

  class P_STU,P_CRS,P_BOK,P_ENR pub
  class I_STU,I_CRS,I_BOK,I_ENR int
  class SHR shr
  class DB db

  style PUB fill:#f8faff,stroke:#3b4a9c
  style INT fill:#fcfcfc,stroke:#aaa,stroke-dasharray:5 4

%% =============================================================================
%% The visibility rule, stated once
%% =============================================================================
%% Spring Modulith treats every direct sub-package of the application package as
%% an application module. Within a module:
%%     module/*            PUBLISHED — any module may import it
%%     module/internal/*   INTERNAL  — only that module may import it
%% ---
%% "internal" is not a magic name; ANY sub-package is internal by default. The
%% name is a convention this project follows so the intent is readable without
%% consulting the tool. If a package genuinely must be published without being
%% flattened into the root, annotate it @NamedInterface — this project does not
%% need that yet, and adding it before it is needed is how a module boundary
%% turns back into a suggestion.
%% ---
%% =============================================================================
%% Consequences worth stating explicitly
%% =============================================================================
%% 1. An ENTITY NEVER LEAVES ITS MODULE. Student lives in student/internal/, so
%%    book and enrollment cannot import it even if they try. They ask
%%    StudentService and get a StudentSummaryResponse. This one rule is what
%%    replaces "the domain layer must not import a DTO" from the pure-DDD
%%    version, and unlike that rule a build failure enforces it.
%% ---
%% 2. A REPOSITORY NEVER LEAVES ITS MODULE either. There is exactly one
%%    JpaRepository per aggregate and only its own service calls it. This is why
%%    the pure-DDD split — a domain repository INTERFACE plus a separate
%%    infrastructure implementation — could be dropped without losing anything:
%%    its purpose was to stop the wrong code depending on Spring Data, and the
%%    module boundary now does that job for free.
%% ---
%% 3. A VALUE OBJECT IS PUBLISHED when another module needs it. StudentId sits
%%    in student/ (root), not student/internal/, precisely because Book.ownerId
%%    is a StudentId. Publishing the identity type and hiding the aggregate is
%%    the mechanical form of rule M1 in module-map.mmd.
%% ---
%% 4. THE LISTENERS ARE INTERNAL. book/internal/StudentDeletedListener imports
%%    student.StudentDeleted — allowed, because book==>student already exists.
%%    Nothing imports the listener. An event handler is an implementation
%%    detail of the module that reacts, never part of its API.
%% ---
%% =============================================================================
%% Reconciling this with req.md §1
%% =============================================================================
%% req.md sketches a flat layout: config / controller / dto / entity /
%% repository / service / exception — grouped by TECHNICAL TYPE. Everything in
%% that list still exists here; it is grouped by MODULE first and type second.
%% ---
%%   req.md            ->  here
%%   controller        ->  <module>/XController              (published)
%%   service           ->  <module>/XService                 (published)
%%   dto               ->  <module>/X{Create,Update}Request, XResponse
%%   entity            ->  <module>/internal/X               (hidden)
%%   repository        ->  <module>/internal/XRepository     (hidden)
%%   exception         ->  shared/ (the thrown types + the handler + envelopes)
%%   config            ->  shared/
%% ---
%% Turning req.md's layout into this one is a rotation, not a redesign: the same
%% classes, cut by feature instead of by type. The reason to prefer it is that a
%% change to "students" touches one directory here and seven there.
%% ---
%% =============================================================================
%% The two departures from req.md, and the trade-off accepted
%% =============================================================================
%% 1. Business rules live ON THE ENTITY where they concern one aggregate
%%    (Book.assignTo enforces the single-owner invariant) and in the SERVICE
%%    where they need a repository (EnrollmentService checks for a duplicate
%%    enrollment). @Service does not become a bag of procedures.
%% ---
%% 2. The domain aggregate IS the JPA entity — one class, annotated @Entity,
%%    with @Convert-ed value objects. Strict hexagonal would keep a persistence-
%%    ignorant aggregate and a separate @Entity with a mapper between them; for
%%    a system this size that doubles the class count for no benefit.
%% ---
%%    The cost: the entity depends on jakarta.persistence. That is an accepted,
%%    documented trade-off. The rules that still hold and that a reviewer should
%%    enforce:
%%      - no @Transactional on an entity — the service owns the boundary
%%      - no DTO type imported by an entity
%%      - no @ManyToOne or @ManyToMany to another aggregate root — identity only
%%      - the entity stays in internal/, so no other module can be coupled to it
%% ---
%%    If true persistence-ignorance is ever needed, it is a change WITHIN one
%%    module: split X into X and internal/XJpaEntity plus a mapper. No other
%%    module notices, because no other module could see the entity to begin
%%    with. That containment is the practical argument for the whole layout.

Sequences

Assign Book

sequences/assign-book.mmd

Sequence: Assign Book to Student

Mermaid source 
%% Sequence: Assign Book to Student
%% Contract: POST /students/{studentId}/books/{bookId}  (operationId assignBookToStudent)
%% Success 200 BookResponse | 404 student or book missing | 409 already owned by another
%% ---
%% This is the diagram to read for how a CROSS-MODULE CALL works, as opposed to
%% a cross-module event. The book module needs to know a student exists; it asks
%% the student module's published service and gets a boolean. It does not — and
%% cannot — touch StudentRepository or the Student entity, both of which live in
%% student/internal/.
%% ---
%% Contrast delete-student.mmd: there, the DOWNSTREAM module reacts to the
%% upstream one, so it must be an event. Here the UPSTREAM answer is needed
%% before proceeding, so it is a direct call along the declared book==>student
%% dependency.

sequenceDiagram
  autonumber
  actor Admin as Library Admin

  box rgb(238, 255, 238) module: book
    participant C as StudentBookController
    participant S as BookOwnershipService
    participant BR as BookRepository
    participant B as Book «Aggregate»
  end

  box rgb(238, 238, 255) module: student
    participant SS as StudentService
  end

  Admin->>C: POST /students/{studentId}/books/{bookId}
  C->>S: assignBook(StudentId, BookId)

  activate S
  Note over S: @Transactional boundary opens here

  S->>SS: exists(studentId)
  Note over SS: published cross-module API. Returns a boolean.<br/>The Student entity never crosses the boundary.
  SS-->>S: false
  alt student not found
    S-->>C: throw ResourceNotFoundException
    C-->>Admin: 404 ErrorResponse (code STUDENT_NOT_FOUND)
  else student exists
    S->>BR: findById(bookId.value())
    BR-->>S: Optional.empty()
    alt book not found
      S-->>C: throw ResourceNotFoundException
      C-->>Admin: 404 ErrorResponse (code BOOK_NOT_FOUND)
    else book found

      rect rgb(235, 250, 235)
        Note over S,B: The single-owner invariant is enforced BY THE AGGREGATE.<br/>The service does not check first and then set — it just asks<br/>the book to change, and the book refuses if it may not.
        S->>B: assignTo(studentId)
        alt owned by a different student
          B-->>S: throw InvalidRelationshipException
          S-->>C: propagate
          C-->>Admin: 409 ErrorResponse (code BOOK_ALREADY_ASSIGNED)
        else unowned, or already owned by this same student
          B-->>S: ownerId := studentId
          S->>BR: save(book)
          BR-->>S: persisted (books.student_id = studentId)
          Note over S: @Transactional boundary commits here
          S-->>C: BookResponse
          C-->>Admin: 200 BookResponse
        end
      end
    end
  end
  deactivate S

  Note over B: Single-owner invariant. Re-assigning to the SAME owner is<br/>idempotent and returns 200. Re-assigning to a DIFFERENT owner is a<br/>conflict, never a silent overwrite.

%% =============================================================================
%% Where the rule lives, and why it moved
%% =============================================================================
%% The pure-DDD version put this in a stateless OwnershipPolicy «DomainService»
%% with assertAssignable(book, candidate), called by the service just before
%% book.assignTo(). The policy read nothing but the book's own ownerId — so the
%% book can enforce it directly:
%% ---
%%   public void assignTo(StudentId newOwner) {
%%       if (isOwned() && !isOwnedBy(newOwner)) {
%%           throw new InvalidRelationshipException(
%%               "BOOK_ALREADY_ASSIGNED", "Book is already assigned to another student");
%%       }
%%       this.ownerId = newOwner;      // same-owner re-assign falls through: idempotent
%%   }
%% ---
%% This is strictly better than the policy: an aggregate that guards its own
%% invariant cannot be bypassed by a caller who forgets to consult the guard.
%% The policy could be — and a forgotten assertAssignable() was a silent
%% overwrite. Compare EnrollmentService in enroll.mmd, where the equivalent rule
%% CANNOT move onto the entity because it needs a repository.
%% ---
%% =============================================================================
%% Why the student existence check is a call and not an event
%% =============================================================================
%% Events are for telling other modules that something HAPPENED. This is a
%% question that must be answered before anything happens, so it is a call. It
%% travels along book ==> student, already declared in
%% ../modules/module-map.mmd — the same edge Book.ownerId : StudentId uses.
%% No new coupling is introduced by this operation.
%% ---
%% Note the direction: book depends on student, never the reverse. There is no
%% StudentService.assignBook() and there never will be, because that would make
%% student import book and close the cycle.
%% ---
%% =============================================================================
%% Concurrency — the one transition this design does not fully pin down
%% =============================================================================
%% Two simultaneous assigns of the same UNOWNED book to different students both
%% read ownerId == null, both pass assignTo(), and both UPDATE. The loser
%% silently overwrites the winner. Options, in increasing order of cost:
%%   - accept last-write-wins and document it (current position)
%%   - @Version on Book -> optimistic locking -> the loser gets an
%%     OptimisticLockException, mapped to 409
%%   - SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the book row (@Lock(PESSIMISTIC_WRITE))
%% Unlike the uniqueness rules, there is no database constraint that can catch
%% this one, because "at most one owner" is already satisfied by a single
%% nullable column. See ../states/book-ownership.mmd.

Create Student

sequences/create-student.mmd

Sequence: Create Student

Mermaid source 
%% Sequence: Create Student
%% Contract: POST /students  (operationId createStudent)
%% Success 201 StudentResponse + Location header
%% 400 bean-validation failure | 409 duplicate studentCode or email
%% ---
%% Representative of the create flow for all three aggregates — Create Book
%% (duplicate isbn) and Create Course (duplicate courseCode, credits > 0)
%% follow the identical shape in their own modules.
%% ---
%% Everything here happens INSIDE the student module. No cross-module call, no
%% event. This is what most of the 23 operations look like; the interesting
%% cross-module ones are delete-student, assign-book, enroll and get-book-owner.

sequenceDiagram
  autonumber
  actor Admin as Academic Admin

  box rgb(238, 238, 255) module: student
    participant C as StudentController
    participant V as Bean Validation
    participant S as StudentService
    participant SR as StudentRepository
    participant St as Student «Aggregate»
  end

  Admin->>C: POST /students { studentCode, firstName, lastName, email, dateOfBirth }

  C->>V: @Valid StudentCreateRequest
  V-->>C: field violations
  alt payload invalid
    C-->>Admin: 400 ValidationErrorResponse { fieldErrors }
  else payload valid
    C->>S: createStudent(StudentCreateRequest)

    activate S
    Note over S: @Transactional boundary opens here

    S->>SR: existsByStudentCode(StudentCode.of(raw))
    SR-->>S: true
    alt studentCode taken
      S-->>C: throw DuplicateResourceException
      C-->>Admin: 409 ErrorResponse (code STUDENT_CODE_EXISTS)
    else studentCode free
      S->>SR: existsByEmail(Email.of(raw))
      SR-->>S: true
      alt email taken
        S-->>C: throw DuplicateResourceException
        C-->>Admin: 409 ErrorResponse (code EMAIL_EXISTS)
      else email free
        S->>St: new Student(StudentCode.of(..), Email.of(..), ..)
        Note over St: value-object factories re-check format.<br/>createdAt / updatedAt set by JPA auditing.
        St-->>S: Student
        S->>SR: save(student)
        SR-->>S: persisted with generated id
        Note over S: @Transactional boundary commits here.<br/>The aggregate does not leave the service — the mapper<br/>turns it into a StudentResponse first.
        S-->>C: StudentResponse
        C-->>Admin: 201 StudentResponse<br/>Location: /api/v1/students/{id}
      end
    end
    deactivate S
  end

  Note over SR: Uniqueness is checked in the service AND enforced by UNIQUE<br/>constraints on students(student_code) and students(email). A race that<br/>slips past the check surfaces as DataIntegrityViolationException, which<br/>GlobalExceptionHandler maps to the same 409 — never a 500.

%% =============================================================================
%% Applies unchanged to
%% =============================================================================
%%   POST /books    UC15  book module    existsByIsbn        -> 409 ISBN_EXISTS
%%   POST /courses  UC11  course module  existsByCourseCode  -> 409 COURSE_CODE_EXISTS
%%                                       plus credits > 0, enforced by @Positive (400)
%% ---
%% Traceability rows 1, 6 and 11 all point here.
%% ---
%% =============================================================================
%% Value objects at the boundary
%% =============================================================================
%% The request DTO carries plain Strings, annotated with @NotBlank / @Email /
%% @Pattern so a malformed payload is a 400 before the service is entered. The
%% service converts them with StudentCode.of() / Email.of(), which re-check the
%% same shapes and throw if given something impossible.
%% ---
%% The duplication is intentional and the two checks answer to different
%% callers: bean validation protects the HTTP contract (a client sent nonsense
%% -> 400 with fieldErrors), the factory protects the aggregate (any caller,
%% including a test or a future listener, cannot construct an invalid Student).
%% Only the first is reachable through the API, which is why the factory throwing
%% is a 500-shaped bug rather than a documented 400.
%% ---
%% Persistence: StudentCode and Email reach the database through
%% StudentCodeConverter and EmailConverter (AttributeConverter), so
%% students.student_code and students.email stay plain VARCHAR columns and the
%% UNIQUE constraints above work normally. See ../classes/class-diagram.mmd.
%% ---
%% =============================================================================
%% A new student owns nothing
%% =============================================================================
%% StudentCreateRequest carries no books and no courses, and cannot. Ownership
%% and enrollment are created by their own operations in their own modules
%% (assign-book.mmd, enroll.mmd) — there is no way to reach across a module
%% boundary from inside a create.

Delete Book

sequences/delete-book.mmd

Sequence: Delete Book

Mermaid source 
%% Sequence: Delete Book
%% Contract: DELETE /books/{bookId}  (operationId deleteBook)
%% Success 204 | 404 book missing
%% The owning Student survives. Ownership disappears with the book. (req.md §16)
%% ---
%% The simplest delete in the system, and worth reading immediately after
%% delete-student.mmd for the contrast: no event, no listener, no cleanup step,
%% no cross-module anything.

sequenceDiagram
  autonumber
  actor Admin as Library Admin

  box rgb(238, 255, 238) module: book
    participant C as BookController
    participant S as BookService
    participant BR as BookRepository
  end

  Admin->>C: DELETE /books/{bookId}
  C->>S: deleteBook(BookId)

  activate S
  Note over S: @Transactional boundary opens here

  S->>BR: existsById(bookId.value())
  BR-->>S: false
  alt book not found
    S-->>C: throw ResourceNotFoundException
    C-->>Admin: 404 ErrorResponse (code BOOK_NOT_FOUND)
  else book exists
    S->>BR: deleteById(bookId.value())
    BR-->>S: removed
    Note over S: @Transactional boundary commits here
    S-->>C: void
    C-->>Admin: 204 No Content
  end
  deactivate S

  Note over S,BR: No ownership cleanup step is needed. ownerId lives ON the Book<br/>aggregate (books.student_id), so deleting the row removes the link<br/>atomically. Contrast delete-student.mmd, where the link lives on the<br/>OTHER side and must be released explicitly, by two other modules.

%% =============================================================================
%% Why this one publishes no event
%% =============================================================================
%% A module publishes a deletion event when SOMETHING ELSE holds a reference to
%% the row being removed:
%% ---
%%   delete a STUDENT   books.student_id and student_courses.student_id point at
%%                      it -> StudentDeleted, two listeners
%%   delete a COURSE    student_courses.course_id points at it
%%                      -> CourseDeleted, one listener
%%   delete a BOOK      NOTHING points at a book -> no event, no listener
%% ---
%% This is the whole rule, and it is a property of the schema rather than a
%% design preference: look at which foreign keys reference the table you are
%% deleting from. See ../../database/schema.mermaid.
%% ---
%% =============================================================================
%% The owner is not consulted
%% =============================================================================
%% Deleting an owned book does not notify, lock, or even read the student who
%% owns it. The book module never calls StudentService here. From the student's
%% side nothing observable changes, because Student has no collection of books —
%% "which books does this student own?" is answered by querying the book module
%% (GET /students/{id}/books), not by reading a field on Student.
%% ---
%% That asymmetry is rule M1 (identity-only references) paying off: a one-sided
%% relationship only ever needs cleaning up from the side that stores it.
%% ---
%% =============================================================================
%% Tests this diagram implies
%% =============================================================================
%%   delete an UNOWNED book  -> 204, row gone
%%   delete an OWNED book    -> 204, row gone, the owning student still exists
%%                              and is unchanged
%%   delete a non-existent book -> 404 BOOK_NOT_FOUND
%%   assert no StudentDeleted / CourseDeleted-style event is published
%% ---
%% See ../states/book-ownership.mmd — both terminal transitions ([*]) are this
%% operation, reachable from Unowned and from Owned alike.

Delete Course

sequences/delete-course.mmd

Sequence: Delete Course (cross-module cleanup by synchronous domain event)

Mermaid source 
%% Sequence: Delete Course (cross-module cleanup by synchronous domain event)
%% Contract: DELETE /courses/{courseId}  (operationId deleteCourse)
%% Success 204 | 404 course missing
%% Enrollments for the course are removed. Students survive. (req.md §16)
%% ---
%% The same shape as delete-student.mmd with one reactor instead of two. Read
%% that diagram first — its footer carries the ordering rule that both obey, and
%% it is not repeated here in full.

sequenceDiagram
  autonumber
  actor Admin as Academic Admin

  box rgb(238, 238, 255) module: course
    participant C as CourseController
    participant S as CourseService
    participant CR as CourseRepository
    participant EV as ApplicationEventPublisher
  end

  box rgb(255, 244, 224) module: enrollment
    participant EL as EnrollmentCleanupListener
    participant ER as EnrollmentRepository
  end

  Admin->>C: DELETE /courses/{courseId}
  C->>S: deleteCourse(CourseId)

  activate S
  Note over S: @Transactional boundary opens here

  S->>CR: findById(courseId.value())
  CR-->>S: Optional.empty()
  alt course not found
    S-->>C: throw ResourceNotFoundException
    C-->>Admin: 404 ErrorResponse (code COURSE_NOT_FOUND)
  else course exists

    rect rgb(245, 245, 255)
      Note over S,EV: Step 1 — publish the fact, BEFORE removing the row
      S->>EV: publishEvent(new CourseDeleted(courseId))
      Note over EV: plain @EventListener — synchronous, same thread,<br/>same transaction. Returns only when the listener is done.
    end

    rect rgb(255, 248, 235)
      Note over EV,ER: Step 2 — the enrollment module reacts
      EV->>EL: on(CourseDeleted)
      activate EL
      EL->>ER: deleteByIdCourseId(courseId.value())
      ER-->>EL: n rows removed
      EL-->>EV: return
      deactivate EL
    end

    EV-->>S: listener complete

    rect rgb(250, 240, 235)
      Note over S,CR: Step 3 — only NOW remove the course row
      S->>CR: delete(course)
      CR-->>S: removed
    end

    Note over S: @Transactional boundary commits here
    S-->>C: void
    C-->>Admin: 204 No Content
  end
  deactivate S

  Note over S,ER: Students enrolled in the course are NOT deleted — only their<br/>student_courses rows for this course. Mirrors delete-student.mmd:<br/>the join rows always die with either parent, and the parents never<br/>cascade into each other.

%% =============================================================================
%% Why the ordering matters here too
%% =============================================================================
%% student_courses.course_id is a foreign key to courses.id with no cascade, so
%% the enrollments must be gone before the course row is. Publishing the event
%% BEFORE CR.delete() and listening with a PLAIN @EventListener is what
%% guarantees that. @TransactionalEventListener(BEFORE_COMMIT) and
%% @ApplicationModuleListener both run too late — the full explanation is in the
%% footer of delete-student.mmd and is not duplicated here on purpose: there is
%% one rule, not two.
%% ---
%% =============================================================================
%% Symmetry worth noticing
%% =============================================================================
%%   delete a STUDENT  -> two reactors: book (release) + enrollment (delete)
%%   delete a COURSE   -> one reactor:  enrollment (delete)
%%   delete a BOOK     -> NO reactor at all — see delete-book.mmd
%% ---
%% The asymmetry is not arbitrary: a module needs an event only when something
%% ELSE holds a reference to the row being removed. books.student_id points at a
%% student, student_courses points at both — so those get events. Nothing points
%% at a book, so deleting one is a plain delete.
%% ---
%% =============================================================================
%% Tests this diagram implies
%% =============================================================================
%%   delete a course with 3 enrolled students
%%       -> 204; all 3 students still exist; 0 student_courses rows for the
%%          course; course row gone
%%   delete a course with no enrollments  -> 204, listener no-ops
%%   delete a non-existent course         -> 404 COURSE_NOT_FOUND, no event
%% ---
%% See also ../states/enrollment.mmd — this is one of the four operations that
%% can end an enrollment.

Delete Student

sequences/delete-student.mmd

Sequence: Delete Student (cross-module cleanup by synchronous domain event)

Mermaid source 
%% Sequence: Delete Student (cross-module cleanup by synchronous domain event)
%% Contract: DELETE /students/{studentId}  (operationId deleteStudent)
%% Success 204 | 404 student missing
%% Books survive as unowned. Courses survive. Only enrollments are destroyed.
%% ---
%% THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT DIAGRAM IN THE SET. It is the only operation whose
%% effects cross three modules, and the ORDER of those effects is a correctness
%% requirement, not a style choice. Read the ordering note at the bottom before
%% implementing anything.
%% ---
%% HOW TO READ IT
%%   Three participant groups, one per module: student (the publisher), book and
%%   enrollment (the reactors). The student module NEVER calls book or
%%   enrollment. It publishes a fact and Spring delivers it. That is the whole
%%   reason student==>book and student==>enrollment do not exist in
%%   ../modules/module-map.mmd, and why the graph stays acyclic.

sequenceDiagram
  autonumber
  actor Admin as Academic Admin

  box rgb(238, 238, 255) module: student
    participant C as StudentController
    participant S as StudentService
    participant SR as StudentRepository
    participant EV as ApplicationEventPublisher
  end

  box rgb(238, 255, 238) module: book
    participant BL as StudentDeletedListener
    participant BR as BookRepository
    participant B as Book «Aggregate»
  end

  box rgb(255, 244, 224) module: enrollment
    participant EL as EnrollmentCleanupListener
    participant ER as EnrollmentRepository
  end

  Admin->>C: DELETE /students/{studentId}
  C->>S: deleteStudent(StudentId)

  activate S
  Note over S: @Transactional boundary opens here.<br/>Everything below commits or rolls back together —<br/>including the work done inside the listeners.

  S->>SR: findById(studentId.value())
  SR-->>S: Optional.empty()
  alt student not found
    S-->>C: throw ResourceNotFoundException
    C-->>Admin: 404 ErrorResponse (code STUDENT_NOT_FOUND)
  else student exists

    rect rgb(245, 245, 255)
      Note over S,EV: Step 1 — publish the fact, BEFORE removing the row
      S->>EV: publishEvent(new StudentDeleted(studentId))
      Note over EV: plain @EventListener -> Spring dispatches SYNCHRONOUSLY,<br/>inline, on this thread, in this transaction.<br/>publishEvent() does not return until every listener has finished.
    end

    rect rgb(235, 250, 235)
      Note over EV,B: Step 2a — the book module reacts: release ownership
      EV->>BL: on(StudentDeleted)
      activate BL
      BL->>BR: findByOwnerId(studentId)
      BR-->>BL: List~Book~
      loop for each owned book
        BL->>B: release()
        B-->>BL: ownerId := null
      end
      BL->>BR: saveAll(books)
      BR-->>BL: persisted (books.student_id = NULL)
      BL-->>EV: return
      deactivate BL
    end

    rect rgb(255, 248, 235)
      Note over EV,ER: Step 2b — the enrollment module reacts: drop enrollments
      EV->>EL: on(StudentDeleted)
      activate EL
      EL->>ER: deleteByIdStudentId(studentId.value())
      ER-->>EL: n rows removed
      EL-->>EV: return
      deactivate EL
    end

    EV-->>S: all listeners complete

    rect rgb(250, 240, 235)
      Note over S,SR: Step 3 — only NOW remove the student row
      S->>SR: delete(student)
      SR-->>S: removed
    end

    Note over S: @Transactional boundary commits here
    S-->>C: void
    C-->>Admin: 204 No Content
  end
  deactivate S

%% =============================================================================
%% THE ORDERING RULE — why this is a plain @EventListener and nothing else
%% =============================================================================
%% books.student_id is a real foreign key to students.id, and there is no
%% ON DELETE CASCADE and no ON DELETE SET NULL in the schema. So every book must
%% be released, and every enrollment removed, BEFORE the student row is deleted.
%% Exactly one of the three obvious mechanisms gets that right:
%% ---
%%   @EventListener                                       <- THIS PROJECT
%%     Dispatched inline by publishEvent(), on the caller's thread, inside the
%%     caller's transaction. The listeners run BEFORE the next statement of
%%     deleteStudent(), which is the delete. Correct order, one transaction, one
%%     rollback. A listener that throws aborts the whole delete — which is what
%%     you want.
%% ---
%%   @TransactionalEventListener(phase = BEFORE_COMMIT)   <- WRONG HERE
%%     Does not run at publishEvent(). It runs at COMMIT — after
%%     SR.delete(student) has already been flushed. The books still point at a
%%     row that is on its way out, and the FK fires. "Before commit" sounds
%%     early enough; it is not, because the delete happened before the commit
%%     too.
%% ---
%%   @ApplicationModuleListener                           <- WRONG HERE
%%     = @Async + @TransactionalEventListener(AFTER_COMMIT)
%%       + @Transactional(propagation = REQUIRES_NEW).
%%     A separate transaction on a separate thread, starting after this one has
%%     already committed the delete. The commit itself would fail on the FK.
%%     Adopting it would mean making books.student_id ON DELETE SET NULL,
%%     accepting a window where enrollments outlive their student, and adding
%%     spring-modulith-starter-jpa plus the event_publication outbox table to
%%     get retries. That is a real architecture and this project does not need
%%     it — see the closing note of ../modules/module-map.mmd.
%% ---
%% Naming: the event is called StudentDeleted although it is published just
%% BEFORE the row disappears. Within the transaction that is a distinction
%% without a difference — if any listener throws, the delete never happens and
%% no observer ever sees the event. Naming it StudentDeletionRequested would
%% describe the mechanism rather than the fact, and the fact is what modules
%% subscribe to.
%% ---
%% =============================================================================
%% What this replaces, if you have read the pure-DDD version
%% =============================================================================
%% There, one StudentApplicationService reached directly into BookRepository and
%% EnrollmentRepository and performed all three steps itself. Same transaction,
%% same order, same result — but it required the student code to import two
%% other modules' repositories, which is precisely the coupling the module
%% boundary now forbids. The event does not change WHAT happens; it changes WHO
%% KNOWS about it. student stays ignorant of both books and enrollments.
%% ---
%% =============================================================================
%% Tests this diagram implies
%% =============================================================================
%%   delete a student who owns 2 books and has 3 enrollments
%%       -> 204; both books still exist with student_id NULL;
%%          0 rows in student_courses for that student; student row gone
%%   delete a student with no books and no enrollments   -> 204, listeners no-op
%%   delete a non-existent student                       -> 404 STUDENT_NOT_FOUND,
%%                                                          no event published
%%   force the book listener to throw
%%       -> the whole transaction rolls back: the student is STILL THERE and
%%          no book was released. This is the test that proves the listeners
%%          share the publisher's transaction; without it the design claim in
%%          this footer is unverified.
%% ---
%% See also ../states/book-ownership.mmd (this is one of four transitions that
%% end an ownership) and ../states/enrollment.mmd.

Enroll

sequences/enroll.mmd

Sequence: Enroll Student in Course

Mermaid source 
%% Sequence: Enroll Student in Course
%% Contract: POST /students/{studentId}/courses/{courseId}  (operationId enrollStudentInCourse)
%% Success 201 EnrollmentResponse | 404 student or course missing | 409 already enrolled
%% ---
%% The enrollment module is the only one that depends on TWO peers, so this is
%% the diagram where the module graph is most visible: two cross-module calls,
%% both read-only, both returning primitives, before any local work happens.

sequenceDiagram
  autonumber
  actor Admin as Academic Admin

  box rgb(255, 244, 224) module: enrollment
    participant C as StudentCourseController
    participant S as EnrollmentService
    participant ER as EnrollmentRepository
    participant E as Enrollment «Aggregate»
  end

  box rgb(238, 238, 255) module: student
    participant SS as StudentService
  end

  box rgb(238, 238, 255) module: course
    participant CS as CourseService
  end

  Admin->>C: POST /students/{studentId}/courses/{courseId}
  C->>S: enroll(StudentId, CourseId)

  activate S
  Note over S: @Transactional boundary opens here

  S->>SS: exists(studentId)
  SS-->>S: false
  alt student not found
    S-->>C: throw ResourceNotFoundException
    C-->>Admin: 404 ErrorResponse (code STUDENT_NOT_FOUND)
  else student exists
    S->>CS: exists(courseId)
    CS-->>S: false
    alt course not found
      S-->>C: throw ResourceNotFoundException
      C-->>Admin: 404 ErrorResponse (code COURSE_NOT_FOUND)
    else course exists

      rect rgb(255, 248, 235)
        Note over S,ER: The no-duplicate-enrolment invariant. It lives in the SERVICE,<br/>not on the entity, because answering it needs a repository.
        S->>ER: existsById(new EnrollmentId(studentId, courseId))
        ER-->>S: true
        alt already enrolled
          S-->>C: throw DuplicateResourceException
          C-->>Admin: 409 ErrorResponse (code ALREADY_ENROLLED)
        else not yet enrolled
          S->>E: Enrollment.open(studentId, courseId)
          E-->>S: id := (studentId, courseId), enrolledAt := now()
          S->>ER: save(enrollment)
          ER-->>S: persisted
          Note over S: @Transactional boundary commits here
          S-->>C: EnrollmentResponse
          C-->>Admin: 201 EnrollmentResponse
        end
      end
    end
  end
  deactivate S

  Note over S,ER: Checked in the service AND backed by the composite PRIMARY KEY on<br/>student_courses(student_id, course_id), so a concurrent insert surfaces<br/>as the same 409 rather than a 500.

%% =============================================================================
%% Why this rule did NOT move onto the aggregate
%% =============================================================================
%% assign-book.mmd moved the single-owner rule out of a policy and onto
%% Book.assignTo(), because the book could answer the question from its own
%% state. This rule cannot make that move: "is this pair already enrolled?" is a
%% question about the TABLE, not about the Enrollment being created. An entity
%% that holds a repository is not an entity.
%% ---
%% So the two modules land in different places on purpose:
%%   book        invariant on the AGGREGATE   (reads its own state)
%%   enrollment  invariant in the SERVICE     (needs a repository)
%% ---
