%% Being able to explain that difference is worth more than the consistency of
%% putting both in a policy class, which is what the pure-DDD version did.
%% EnrollmentPolicy.assertNotEnrolled() held a repository and a throw, and it
%% was called from exactly one place.
%% ---
%% =============================================================================
%% Two cross-module calls, zero cross-module writes
%% =============================================================================
%% enrollment reads from student and course; it never writes to either, and
%% neither knows this operation happened. The enrollment row is the only thing
%% created, and it lives in the enrollment module's own table. No event is
%% published, because nothing downstream needs to react — see the symmetry note
%% in delete-course.mmd.
%% ---
%% Both calls return a boolean rather than an entity. StudentService.exists()
%% and CourseService.exists() are published precisely so that this module never
%% needs to see a Student or a Course, both of which are internal to their own
%% modules and unreachable from here.
%% ---
%% =============================================================================
%% Status code: 201, not 200
%% =============================================================================
%% Enrolling CREATES a resource — a row in student_courses with its own
%% enrolledAt. Contrast assign-book.mmd, which returns 200 because it modifies
%% an existing Book rather than creating anything. Both are POST; the status
%% codes differ because the effects do.

Get Book Owner

sequences/get-book-owner.mmd

Sequence: Get Owner of a Book

Mermaid source 
%% Sequence: Get Owner of a Book
%% Contract: GET /books/{bookId}/owner  (operationId getBookOwner)
%% Success 200 StudentSummaryResponse | 404 book missing OR book unowned
%% ---
%% Two distinct 404 causes share one status code — they are separated by the
%% `code` field of ErrorResponse so clients can tell them apart. (req.md §7)
%% ---
%% Also the one read in the system that crosses a module boundary to build its
%% response body: the book module owns the ownership link, the student module
%% owns everything a caller wants to know about the owner.

sequenceDiagram
  autonumber
  actor Client as API Client

  box rgb(238, 255, 238) module: book
    participant C as BookController
    participant S as BookOwnershipService
    participant BR as BookRepository
    participant B as Book «Aggregate»
  end

  box rgb(238, 238, 255) module: student
    participant SS as StudentService
  end

  Client->>C: GET /books/{bookId}/owner
  C->>S: findOwner(BookId)

  activate S
  Note over S: @Transactional(readOnly = true)

  S->>BR: findById(bookId.value())
  BR-->>S: Optional.empty()
  alt book not found
    S-->>C: throw ResourceNotFoundException
    C-->>Client: 404 ErrorResponse (code BOOK_NOT_FOUND)
  else book found
    S->>B: isOwned()
    B-->>S: false
    alt book has no owner
      S-->>C: throw ResourceNotFoundException
      C-->>Client: 404 ErrorResponse (code BOOK_NOT_ASSIGNED)<br/>"Book is not assigned to any student"
    else book has an owner
      B-->>S: ownerId : StudentId
      S->>SS: summaryOf(ownerId)
      Note over SS: published cross-module API.<br/>Returns a DTO assembled inside the student module —<br/>the Student entity never crosses the boundary.
      SS-->>S: Optional~StudentSummaryResponse~
      Note over S: read-only, nothing to commit
      S-->>C: StudentSummaryResponse
      C-->>Client: 200 StudentSummaryResponse
    end
  end
  deactivate S

  Note over C: 404 was chosen over "200 with null body" per req.md §7, so that<br/>"no such book" and "book has no owner" are both absences rather than<br/>one absence and one null-valued success.

%% =============================================================================
%% The response body is built by the OTHER module
%% =============================================================================
%% StudentSummaryResponse { id, studentCode, firstName, lastName } is a type
%% published by the student module, and StudentService.summaryOf() is the method
%% that fills it. The book module receives it finished and passes it through.
%% ---
%% This is the pattern for every cross-module read in the system, and the reason
%% it is safe: the book module cannot import Student, cannot import
%% StudentRepository, and therefore cannot accidentally start depending on the
%% student table's shape. If StudentSummaryResponse ever needs a new field, the
%% student module adds it and nothing here changes.
%% ---
%% =============================================================================
%% The empty Optional that should be impossible
%% =============================================================================
%% summaryOf(ownerId) returns an Optional. If books.student_id is a valid FK, an
%% owned book's owner always exists and the Optional is always present.
%% ---
%% Treat an empty one as a 500, not a 404: it means the FK was violated or a
%% student was deleted without the StudentDeleted listener releasing their
%% books — i.e. delete-student.mmd is broken. Silently returning 404
%% BOOK_NOT_ASSIGNED there would hide a data-integrity bug behind a normal-
%% looking response.
%% ---
%% =============================================================================
%% Why these two 404s DO get different codes
%% =============================================================================
%%   BOOK_NOT_FOUND      the caller has the wrong book id — fix the request
%%   BOOK_NOT_ASSIGNED   the book is real and simply has no owner — assign one
%% ---
%% Two different next actions, so two different codes. Contrast
%% unassign-book.mmd, where "unowned" and "owned by someone else" share
%% OWNERSHIP_NOT_FOUND because the caller's next action is the same either way.
%% This operation and that one are the only two places in the contract where the
%% `code` field is doing real work — see ../traceability.md.

List Students

sequences/list-students.mmd

Sequence: List Students (paged · sorted · searched)

Mermaid source 
%% Sequence: List Students (paged · sorted · searched)
%% Contract: GET /students  (operationId getStudents)
%% Success 200 PageStudentResponse | 400 malformed paging parameter
%% ---
%% Representative of EVERY paged read in the contract — GET /books (UC17) and
%% GET /courses (UC8) are the identical shape in their own modules, with their
%% own repository and Page*Response. Traceability rows 2, 7 and 12 point here.
%% ---
%% This flow has NO rule to enforce and NO 404: an empty result is 200 with an
%% empty content array, never "not found". That is the whole reason it deserves
%% its own diagram instead of being read as a variant of create-student.mmd.

sequenceDiagram
  autonumber
  actor Client as API Client

  box rgb(238, 238, 255) module: student
    participant C as StudentController
    participant S as StudentService
    participant SR as StudentRepository
    participant M as StudentMapper
  end

  participant PR as Spring MVC<br/>PageableHandlerMethodArgumentResolver

  Client->>C: GET /students?page=0&size=20&sort=lastName,asc&search=john

  C->>PR: bind page / size / sort
  Note over PR: page >= 0 (default 0), 1 <= size <= 100 (default 20),<br/>sort is "property,(asc|desc)" — see<br/>api-contract/components/parameters/
  PR-->>C: Pageable

  alt page/size not an integer, or sort names an unknown property
    C-->>Client: 400 ValidationErrorResponse
  else parameters bind
    C->>S: listStudents(search, Pageable)

    activate S
    Note over S: @Transactional(readOnly = true) — a read boundary,<br/>not a write one. There is no business rule to enforce<br/>on a query.

    S->>SR: search(query, pageable)
    Note over SR: search == null -> findAll(pageable)<br/>search != null -> case-insensitive LIKE over<br/>firstName, lastName, studentCode, email
    SR-->>S: Page~Student~ (content + totalElements + totalPages)

    S->>M: toResponse(each Student)
    M-->>S: List~StudentResponse~
    Note over S: @Transactional boundary closes here.<br/>Aggregates never leave the module — only DTOs do.<br/>Student lives in student/internal/ and nothing outside<br/>this module could receive one anyway.
    S-->>C: PageStudentResponse { content, page: PageMetadata }
    C-->>Client: 200 PageStudentResponse
  end

  Note over C,SR: An out-of-range page (page=99 of 3) is NOT an error: it returns<br/>200 with content: [] and empty: true. Same for a search that matches<br/>nothing. 404 belongs to single-resource reads only.

  Note over S,M: The size cap of 100 is a contract term, not a suggestion. Enforce it<br/>on binding (spring.data.web.pageable.max-page-size) so a caller cannot<br/>ask for the whole table in one request.

%% =============================================================================
%% Applies unchanged to
%% =============================================================================
%%   GET /books    UC17  book module    BookService.listBooks     PageBookResponse
%%   GET /courses  UC8   course module  CourseService.listCourses PageCourseResponse
%% ---
%% PageMetadata is the one response type shared by all three, and it lives in
%% the shared module — it carries no business meaning, only page/size/total.
%% ---
%% =============================================================================
%% Does NOT apply to the relationship reads
%% =============================================================================
%% GET /students/{id}/books, GET /students/{id}/courses and
%% GET /courses/{id}/students return PLAIN ARRAYS, not pages, and they DO 404
%% when the parent id is unknown — that existence check is a cross-module call
%% to StudentService.exists() or CourseService.exists(), drawn as an «include»
%% in ../use-cases/use-cases-includes.mmd. Do not copy this diagram onto them.
%% ---
%% =============================================================================
%% Why the mapper is internal
%% =============================================================================
%% StudentMapper lives in student/internal/ because it is the one class that
%% touches both a Student and a StudentResponse. Publishing it would let another
%% module ask for a Student to be mapped — and to do that, that module would
%% first need a Student, which it cannot obtain. Keeping the mapper internal
%% keeps that impossibility obvious rather than merely true.

Unassign Book

sequences/unassign-book.mmd

Sequence: Unassign Book from Student

Mermaid source 
%% Sequence: Unassign Book from Student
%% Contract: DELETE /students/{studentId}/books/{bookId}  (operationId unassignBookFromStudent)
%% Success 204 | 404 when the student-book relationship does not exist
%% The book itself is NEVER deleted.

sequenceDiagram
  autonumber
  actor Admin as Library Admin

  box rgb(238, 255, 238) module: book
    participant C as StudentBookController
    participant S as BookOwnershipService
    participant BR as BookRepository
    participant B as Book «Aggregate»
  end

  Admin->>C: DELETE /students/{studentId}/books/{bookId}
  C->>S: unassignBook(StudentId, BookId)

  activate S
  Note over S: @Transactional boundary opens here

  S->>BR: findById(bookId.value())
  BR-->>S: Optional.empty()
  alt book not found
    S-->>C: throw ResourceNotFoundException
    C-->>Admin: 404 ErrorResponse (code BOOK_NOT_FOUND)
  else book found
    S->>B: isOwnedBy(studentId)
    B-->>S: false
    alt book unowned, or owned by a different student
      S-->>C: throw ResourceNotFoundException
      C-->>Admin: 404 ErrorResponse (code OWNERSHIP_NOT_FOUND)
    else owned by this student
      B-->>S: true
      S->>B: release()
      B-->>S: ownerId := null
      S->>BR: save(book)
      BR-->>S: persisted (books.student_id = NULL)
      Note over S: @Transactional boundary commits here
      S-->>C: void
      C-->>Admin: 204 No Content
    end
  end
  deactivate S

  Note over BR,B: Only the ownership link is cleared. The Book row survives with<br/>student_id = NULL and remains listable via GET /books.

%% =============================================================================
%% Why the guard is a service `if` and not an aggregate throw
%% =============================================================================
%% assign-book.mmd pushed its rule INTO Book.assignTo(), because refusing a bad
%% assignment protects the book's own invariant. This one is different:
%% release() has no invariant to protect — clearing an already-null owner is
%% harmless, and Book.release() is idempotent by design.
%% ---
%% What is being enforced here is an API contract, not a domain invariant: the
%% caller named a specific student, and if that student is not the owner then
%% the relationship they asked to remove does not exist, so the answer is 404.
%% That is an HTTP-shaped decision, so it belongs in the service beside the
%% other 404s, not inside the aggregate.
%% ---
%% The pure-DDD version routed it through OwnershipPolicy.assertOwnedBy(). The
%% policy read only book.ownerId, so Book.isOwnedBy(StudentId) replaces it — a
%% query method on the aggregate, with the throw left in the service where the
%% status code is decided.
%% ---
%% =============================================================================
%% Two 404s, one code — and why that differs from get-book-owner.mmd
%% =============================================================================
%%   book does not exist                      -> BOOK_NOT_FOUND
%%   book exists but is unowned               -> OWNERSHIP_NOT_FOUND
%%   book exists but is owned by someone else -> OWNERSHIP_NOT_FOUND
%% ---
%% The last two share a code deliberately: from the caller's point of view "this
%% student does not own this book" is one fact, and telling them WHO does own it
%% would leak another student's relationship. get-book-owner.mmd splits its two
%% causes precisely because there the owner is what was asked for.
%% ---
%% =============================================================================
%% No cross-module call
%% =============================================================================
%% Note what is absent: there is no StudentService.exists() here. Ownership is a
%% column on the book, so the book module can answer the whole question alone.
%% If the student id names nobody, no book is owned by it, and the operation
%% 404s with OWNERSHIP_NOT_FOUND without ever consulting the student module.
%% ---
%% See ../states/book-ownership.mmd — this is one of the four transitions that
%% end an ownership.

Unenroll

sequences/unenroll.mmd

Sequence: Unenroll Student from Course

Mermaid source 
%% Sequence: Unenroll Student from Course
%% Contract: DELETE /students/{studentId}/courses/{courseId}  (operationId unenrollStudentFromCourse)
%% Success 204 | 404 when the enrollment does not exist
%% Both the Student and the Course survive.
%% ---
%% The mirror image of enroll.mmd, and notably SHORTER: it makes no cross-module
%% call at all. The composite id (studentId, courseId) is enough to find the
%% row, so neither the student module nor the course module is consulted.

sequenceDiagram
  autonumber
  actor Admin as Academic Admin

  box rgb(255, 244, 224) module: enrollment
    participant C as StudentCourseController
    participant S as EnrollmentService
    participant ER as EnrollmentRepository
  end

  Admin->>C: DELETE /students/{studentId}/courses/{courseId}
  C->>S: unenroll(StudentId, CourseId)

  activate S
  Note over S: @Transactional boundary opens here

  S->>ER: existsById(new EnrollmentId(studentId, courseId))
  ER-->>S: false
  alt enrollment not found
    S-->>C: throw ResourceNotFoundException
    C-->>Admin: 404 ErrorResponse (code ENROLLMENT_NOT_FOUND)
  else enrollment exists
    S->>ER: deleteById(new EnrollmentId(studentId, courseId))
    ER-->>S: 1 row removed
    Note over S: @Transactional boundary commits here
    S-->>C: void
    C-->>Admin: 204 No Content
  end
  deactivate S

  Note over ER: Only the student_courses row is removed.<br/>Neither the Student aggregate nor the Course aggregate is touched —<br/>they are in other modules and this operation cannot reach them.

%% =============================================================================
%% Why there is no existence check on the student or the course
%% =============================================================================
%% enroll.mmd asks StudentService.exists() and CourseService.exists() because it
%% is about to CREATE a row referencing both, and a row referencing a
%% non-existent parent must not be written. Unenroll writes nothing — it removes
%% a row that, if it exists, already proves both parents existed when it was
%% created.
%% ---
%% So the single existsById() covers every 404 case:
%%   student does not exist  -> no enrollment row  -> 404 ENROLLMENT_NOT_FOUND
%%   course does not exist   -> no enrollment row  -> 404 ENROLLMENT_NOT_FOUND
%%   both exist, not enrolled-> no enrollment row  -> 404 ENROLLMENT_NOT_FOUND
%% ---
%% One code for all three is deliberate. The client asked to end a relationship
%% that is not there; WHICH of its two ends is missing is not information the
%% client can act on differently. Contrast get-book-owner.mmd, where the two
%% causes DO get different codes because the client can act on them differently.
%% ---
%% =============================================================================
%% The four ways an enrollment can end
%% =============================================================================
%%   UC12  DELETE /students/{s}/courses/{c}  this diagram        204
%%   UC5   DELETE /students/{s}              delete-student.mmd  204, via event
%%   UC10  DELETE /courses/{c}               delete-course.mmd   204, via event
%%   —     never expires on its own; there is no enrollment lifecycle job
%% ---
%% All of them are in ../states/enrollment.mmd, which is the transition
%% checklist for the state-based tests.

Update Student

sequences/update-student.mmd

Sequence: Update Student

Mermaid source 
%% Sequence: Update Student
%% Contract: PUT /students/{studentId}  (operationId updateStudent)
%% Success 200 StudentResponse
%% 400 bean-validation failure | 404 student missing | 409 code/email taken by ANOTHER student
%% ---
%% Representative of the update flow for all three aggregates — Update Course
%% (courseCode, credits > 0) and Update Book (isbn) follow the identical shape
%% in their own modules. Traceability rows 4, 9 and 14 all point here.
%% ---
%% WHY THIS IS NOT "create-student.mmd with a different verb"
%%   Create asks "does this value exist anywhere?". Update must ask "does this
%%   value exist on a DIFFERENT row?" — a student keeping their own studentCode
%%   must not 409 against themselves. That single word (EXCLUDING SELF) is the
%%   most commonly implemented-wrong rule in this contract, so it gets a view.

sequenceDiagram
  autonumber
  actor Admin as Academic Admin

  box rgb(238, 238, 255) module: student
    participant C as StudentController
    participant V as Bean Validation
    participant S as StudentService
    participant SR as StudentRepository
    participant St as Student «Aggregate»
  end

  Admin->>C: PUT /students/{studentId} { studentCode, firstName, lastName, email, dateOfBirth }

  C->>V: @Valid StudentUpdateRequest
  V-->>C: field violations
  alt payload invalid
    C-->>Admin: 400 ValidationErrorResponse { fieldErrors }
  else payload valid
    C->>S: updateStudent(StudentId, StudentUpdateRequest)

    activate S
    Note over S: @Transactional boundary opens here

    S->>SR: findById(studentId.value())
    SR-->>S: Optional.empty()
    alt student not found
      S-->>C: throw ResourceNotFoundException
      C-->>Admin: 404 ErrorResponse (code STUDENT_NOT_FOUND)
    else student exists

      rect rgb(255, 245, 235)
        Note over S,SR: Uniqueness EXCLUDING SELF — the whole point of this diagram
        S->>SR: existsByStudentCodeAndIdNot(newCode, studentId.value())
        SR-->>S: true
        alt code belongs to another student
          S-->>C: throw DuplicateResourceException
          C-->>Admin: 409 ErrorResponse (code STUDENT_CODE_EXISTS)
        else code free, or unchanged and still this student's own
          S->>SR: existsByEmailAndIdNot(newEmail, studentId.value())
          SR-->>S: true
          alt email belongs to another student
            S-->>C: throw DuplicateResourceException
            C-->>Admin: 409 ErrorResponse (code EMAIL_EXISTS)
          else email free, or unchanged
            S->>St: rename(firstName, lastName)
            S->>St: changeEmail(Email.of(newEmail))
            Note over St: The aggregate mutates ITSELF through behaviour methods.<br/>No setter is called from the service. Value-object<br/>factories re-check format. updatedAt is set by JPA auditing.
            St-->>S: mutated aggregate (still managed by the persistence context)
            S->>SR: save(student)
            SR-->>S: persisted
            Note over S: @Transactional boundary commits here
            S-->>C: StudentResponse
            C-->>Admin: 200 StudentResponse (no Location header — the resource already existed)
          end
        end
      end
    end
    deactivate S
  end

  Note over SR: existsBy*AndIdNot is the exclude-self form of the create-time check.<br/>Written as existsByStudentCode(code) it produces the classic bug:<br/>PUT with an unchanged studentCode 409s against the student's own row.

  Note over S,St: Fields the request must NOT be able to change: id, createdAt,<br/>and — on Book — ownerId. Ownership moves only through UC20/UC21<br/>(assign-book.mmd / unassign-book.mmd), never through an update body.

%% =============================================================================
%% Applies unchanged to
%% =============================================================================
%%   PUT /courses/{id}  UC9   course module  existsByCourseCodeAndIdNot
%%                            -> 409 COURSE_CODE_EXISTS
%%                            plus credits > 0, enforced by @Positive (400)
%%   PUT /books/{id}    UC18  book module    existsByIsbnAndIdNot
%%                            -> 409 ISBN_EXISTS
%%                            ownerId is absent from BookUpdateRequest by design
%% ---
%% =============================================================================
%% No event, no cross-module call
%% =============================================================================
%% An update is entirely local to its module. Nothing outside student cares that
%% a name or an email changed — book stores only a StudentId, and enrollment
%% stores only a StudentId and a CourseId, so no other module holds a copy of
%% anything this operation can modify.
%% ---
%% That is a direct consequence of rule M1 in ../modules/module-map.mmd
%% (identity-only references). Had another module cached the student's name, an
%% update would need a StudentRenamed event and the whole eventual-consistency
%% apparatus that goes with it.
%% ---
%% =============================================================================
%% PUT semantics chosen
%% =============================================================================
%% PUT here is a FULL replace of the mutable fields: every field in
%% StudentUpdateRequest is required, and the whole aggregate state is set from
%% it. There is no PATCH in this contract, so a caller cannot send a partial
%% body — omitting a field is a 400, not "leave it alone".
%% ---
%% Updating with a body identical to the current state is a valid 200, not a
%% 409 and not a 304. It re-saves the row and bumps updatedAt.

State Machines

Book Ownership

states/book-ownership.mmd

State Diagram — Book ownership lifecycle

Mermaid source 
%% State Diagram — Book ownership lifecycle
%% Aggregate: Book «Aggregate»  (application module: book)
%% Invariant under test: a book has AT MOST ONE owner.
%% ---
%% Every transition below is owned by the BOOK module. Ownership is a column on
%% books, so no other module can move a book between these states directly —
%% not even the delete-student transition, which arrives as an event the book
%% module chooses how to handle.
%% ---
%% WHY THIS VIEW EXISTS
%%   The sequence diagrams each show ONE operation. This shows the whole set of
%%   states a single Book can be in and every transition between them, so the
%%   question "what can happen to a book, and from where?" has one answer.
%%   It is also the checklist for the ownership state-transition tests in
%%   plan-springBootTestPlan.prompt.md.
%% ---
%% The state is not a column. `Unowned` and `Owned` are just books.student_id
%% IS NULL / IS NOT NULL. Nothing in the schema stores a status.

stateDiagram-v2
  direction LR

  state "Unowned<br/>ownerId = null<br/>books.student_id IS NULL" as Unowned
  state "Owned<br/>ownerId = StudentId(x)<br/>books.student_id = x" as Owned

  [*] --> Unowned : POST /books (UC15) — 201<br/>a new book is ALWAYS unowned<br/>BookCreateRequest carries no ownerId

  Unowned --> Owned : POST /students/{x}/books/{b} (UC20)<br/>assignTo(x) — 200 BookResponse

  Owned --> Unowned : DELETE /students/{x}/books/{b} (UC21)<br/>release() — 204, the book SURVIVES
  Owned --> Unowned : DELETE /students/{x} (UC5)<br/>release() in the book module's<br/>StudentDeleted listener

  Owned --> Owned : POST /students/{x}/books/{b} again (UC20)<br/>same owner — idempotent, 200
  Owned --> Owned : PUT /books/{b} (UC18)<br/>ownerId is NOT part of BookUpdateRequest

  Unowned --> [*] : DELETE /books/{b} (UC19) — 204
  Owned --> [*] : DELETE /books/{b} (UC19) — 204<br/>ownership dies with the row<br/>the OWNER survives

  note right of Owned
    REJECTED — the invariant at work
    assign Owned(x) to y → 409
    BOOK_ALREADY_ASSIGNED
    unassign an Unowned book → 404
    unassign Owned(x) as y → 404
    both OWNERSHIP_NOT_FOUND
    GET owner of Unowned → 404
    BOOK_NOT_ASSIGNED
  end note

  note left of Unowned
    Unowned is a normal book, not a
    soft-deleted one. Still listable,
    updatable and assignable again.
  end note

%% =============================================================================
%% Transition -> where it is specified
%% =============================================================================
%%   create              ../sequences/create-student.mmd  (create is one shape
%%                                                         for all three aggregates)
%%   assign / re-assign  ../sequences/assign-book.mmd
%%   unassign            ../sequences/unassign-book.mmd
%%   release on delete   ../sequences/delete-student.mmd  (step 2a of 3)
%%   delete book         ../sequences/delete-book.mmd
%%   read the owner      ../sequences/get-book-owner.mmd
%% ---
%% =============================================================================
%% Two facts a reader usually gets wrong
%% =============================================================================
%% 1. Deleting a STUDENT does not delete their books. It moves every book they
%%    own from Owned back to Unowned, inside the same transaction that deletes
%%    the student. The student module does not perform that move and does not
%%    know it happens: it publishes StudentDeleted and the BOOK module's
%%    listener does the release. See ../modules/module-map.mmd rule M3 and the
%%    ordering footer of ../sequences/delete-student.mmd.
%% 2. Deleting a BOOK does not touch the student. Ownership is a column ON THE
%%    BOOK, so the link disappears with the row, no cleanup is needed, and no
%%    event is published at all.
%% ---
%% Concurrency: two simultaneous assigns of the same unowned book to different
%% students both pass Book.assignTo() and race on the UPDATE. The loser must
%% not overwrite the winner — take the book row with an optimistic (@Version) or
%% pessimistic lock in BookOwnershipService, or accept last-write-wins and
%% document it. This is the one transition the current design does not fully pin
%% down; no database constraint can catch it, because "at most one owner" is
%% already satisfied by a single nullable column. See the closing note of
%% ../sequences/assign-book.mmd.

Enrollment

states/enrollment.mmd

State Diagram — Enrollment lifecycle

Mermaid source 
%% State Diagram — Enrollment lifecycle
%% Aggregate: Enrollment «Aggregate»  (application module: enrollment)
%% Identity: the composite (studentId, courseId). Table: student_courses.
%% Invariant under test: no duplicate (studentId, courseId).
%% ---
%% WHY THIS VIEW EXISTS
%%   Enrollment has only two states, but FOUR different operations destroy it,
%%   and only one of them is called "unenroll" — the other three are triggered
%%   from OTHER modules. This is the view that shows all four in one place.
%% ---
%%   Every transition is executed by the ENROLLMENT module. Two of them are
%%   requested by it (UC11, UC12); the other two arrive as domain events from
%%   the student and course modules, which never touch student_courses
%%   themselves. See ../modules/module-map.mmd rule M3.
%% ---
%% Read the states as being about ONE PAIR (studentId=s, courseId=c), not about
%% a student and not about a course.

stateDiagram-v2
  direction LR

  state "Not enrolled<br/>no row in student_courses<br/>for (s, c)" as NotEnrolled
  state "Enrolled<br/>row (s, c) exists<br/>enrolledAt = the instant of Enrollment.open()" as Enrolled

  [*] --> NotEnrolled : both s and c exist as aggregates<br/>(no row is created by creating a student or a course)

  NotEnrolled --> Enrolled : POST /students/{s}/courses/{c} (UC11)<br/>EnrollmentService duplicate check passes<br/>Enrollment.open(s, c) — 201 EnrollmentResponse

  Enrolled --> NotEnrolled : DELETE /students/{s}/courses/{c} (UC12)<br/>existsById passes — 204<br/>BOTH the student and the course survive
  Enrolled --> NotEnrolled : DELETE /students/{s} (UC5)<br/>deleteByIdStudentId, in the enrollment module's<br/>StudentDeleted listener
  Enrolled --> NotEnrolled : DELETE /courses/{c} (UC10)<br/>deleteByIdCourseId, in the enrollment module's<br/>CourseDeleted listener

  note right of Enrolled
    REJECTED — the invariant at work
    enroll again → 409
    ALREADY_ENROLLED
    (no second row, enrolledAt unchanged)
    unenroll when not enrolled → 404
    ENROLLMENT_NOT_FOUND
    unknown student → 404, checked FIRST
    unknown course → 404
  end note

  note left of NotEnrolled
    Not enrolled is the ABSENCE of a row,
    so it is also the state after the
    student or the course is deleted.
    There is no cancelled / suspended /
    completed state — grading is out of
    scope (glossary.md, Scope).
  end note

%% =============================================================================
%% Transition -> where it is specified
%% =============================================================================
%%   enroll              ../sequences/enroll.mmd
%%   unenroll            ../sequences/unenroll.mmd
%%   cleanup on student  ../sequences/delete-student.mmd  (step 2b of 3)
%%   cleanup on course   ../sequences/delete-course.mmd   (step 2 of 3)
%% ---
%% =============================================================================
%% Notes that matter for implementation and for tests
%% =============================================================================
%% 1. enrolledAt is set by Enrollment.open(), NOT by JPA auditing. Re-enrolling
%%    after an unenroll produces a NEW enrolledAt — the pair carries no history.
%% 2. Both event-driven transitions delete rows without loading the Enrollment
%%    aggregate. That is deliberate: the join row has no invariant of its own to
%%    protect on the way out.
%% 3. Ordering is not optional. Enrollments must be removed BEFORE their student
%%    or course row, or the FK is left dangling. This is why both listeners are
%%    plain @EventListener and both events are published BEFORE the parent row
%%    is deleted — the full reasoning is in the footer of
%%    ../sequences/delete-student.mmd, and it is the single most important
%%    implementation detail in this documentation set.
%% 4. Because the listeners run in the publisher's transaction, a failure in
%%    either one rolls the parent delete back. Test that: make the listener
%%    throw and assert the student or course is still there.
%% 5. The 409 is defended twice: the duplicate check in EnrollmentService, and
%%    the composite PRIMARY KEY on student_courses(student_id, course_id) for
%%    the race. Both must exist; the key is currently missing from the schema
%%    because no migration exists at all (../traceability.md, "Implementation
%%    gaps", item 2).

Use Cases Includes

use-cases/use-cases-includes.mmd

«include» view — Student Management

Mermaid source 
%% «include» view — Student Management
%% Companion to use-cases.mmd, which shows actors and use cases only.
%% This view shows the one relationship that genuinely needs arrows: which
%% relationship use cases include which shared existence check.
%% ---
%% HOW TO READ THIS DIAGRAM
%%   Use cases are grouped by the SET of checks they include, so one arrow
%%   speaks for the whole group. That turns 12 crossing «include» lines into 7
%%   short ones. A use case not listed here includes nothing — a plain CRUD
%%   read/write on a single aggregate.
%% ---
%%   The checks are not use cases a user starts; they are the reusable guard
%%   every relationship operation runs first, and the source of its 404.
%% ---
%% EACH CHECK IS A CROSS-MODULE CALL, AND THAT IS THE POINT
%%   "Verify Student Exists" is StudentService.exists(StudentId) — a method the
%%   student module publishes for exactly this purpose. "Verify Course Exists"
%%   is CourseService.exists(CourseId). Both return a boolean; neither lets an
%%   entity cross a module boundary.
%% ---
%%   So this diagram is also the inventory of every cross-module CALL in the
%%   system. Read against ../modules/module-map.mmd, each dotted arrow below is
%%   one of the three solid dependency edges being used:
%%     G_SB -> INC1   book       ==> student     (assign / unassign / list books)
%%     G_S  -> INC1   book       ==> student     (list books of a student)
%%     G_SC -> INC1   enrollment ==> student
%%     G_SC -> INC2   enrollment ==> course
%%     G_C  -> INC2   enrollment ==> course
%%     G_SB -> INC3   book       -> book         (local — not cross-module)
%%     G_B  -> INC3   book       -> book         (local — not cross-module)
%% ---
%%   "Verify Book Exists" is the odd one out: every use case that needs it is
%%   already IN the book module, so it is a plain repository lookup, not a
%%   published API. Nothing outside book/ ever needs to ask whether a book
%%   exists — which is why BookService has no exists() method.

%%{init: {"flowchart": {"rankSpacing": 90, "nodeSpacing": 30}}}%%
flowchart LR

  TITLE["every dotted arrow reads «include»"]:::title

  subgraph G_C["needs: course"]
    direction TB
    UC14([UC14 · List Students in a Course])
  end

  subgraph G_SC["needs: student + course"]
    direction TB
    UC11([UC11 · Enroll Student in Course])
    UC12([UC12 · Unenroll Student from Course])
  end

  subgraph G_S["needs: student"]
    direction TB
    UC13([UC13 · List Courses of a Student])
    UC22([UC22 · List Books Owned by a Student])
  end

  subgraph G_SB["needs: student + book"]
    direction TB
    UC20([UC20 · Assign Book to Student])
    UC21([UC21 · Unassign Book from Student])
  end

  subgraph G_B["needs: book"]
    direction TB
    UC23([UC23 · Get Owner of a Book])
  end

  %% The three shared checks stay OUTSIDE any subgraph on purpose: an arrow
  %% pointing into a container terminates on the container's border, which is
  %% precisely what makes a target unreadable. Plain nodes take the arrowhead
  %% on the node itself.
  INC2([Verify Course Exists<br/>CourseService.exists — published])
  INC1([Verify Student Exists<br/>StudentService.exists — published])
  INC3([Verify Book Exists<br/>BookRepository — local to book/])

  %% Every edge here is «include» — stated once in the title rather than
  %% repeated as seven labels fighting for the same space.
  G_C  -.-> INC2
  G_SC -.-> INC2
  G_SC -.-> INC1
  G_S  -.-> INC1
  G_SB -.-> INC1
  G_SB -.-> INC3
  G_B  -.-> INC3

  classDef mEnrol fill:#fff4e0,stroke:#b8860b,color:#111;
  classDef mBook fill:#e6f6ea,stroke:#2f7d46,color:#111;
  classDef shared fill:#f5f5f5,stroke:#999,color:#111,stroke-dasharray:3 3;
  classDef title fill:#fff,stroke:#fff,color:#777;

  class UC11,UC12,UC13,UC14 mEnrol
  class UC20,UC21,UC22,UC23 mBook
  class INC1,INC2,INC3 shared

%% =============================================================================
%% What each check raises  (see ../traceability.md "Error mapping")
%% =============================================================================
%% Verify Student Exists  ResourceNotFoundException -> 404 STUDENT_NOT_FOUND
%% Verify Course Exists   ResourceNotFoundException -> 404 COURSE_NOT_FOUND
%% Verify Book Exists     ResourceNotFoundException -> 404 BOOK_NOT_FOUND
%% ---
%% Note WHO throws. The published exists() methods return a boolean and throw
%% nothing; the CALLING module turns false into the exception. That keeps the
%% student and course modules ignorant of what their callers consider an error,
%% and it is why exists() returns boolean rather than the aggregate.
%% ---
%% Order matters on the two-check use cases: verify the path's first id first
%% (student before course, student before book) so the 404 a caller gets names
%% the id they actually got wrong.
%% ---
%% UC22 and UC13 return [] — not 404 — when the student exists but owns/enrols
%% in nothing. The include is what makes "missing student" and "empty result"
%% distinguishable.
%% ---
%% =============================================================================
%% The one relationship use case that includes NOTHING
%% =============================================================================
%% UC12 Unenroll appears in G_SC above for symmetry with UC11, but see
%% ../sequences/unenroll.mmd: it can skip both checks, because the existence of
%% the enrollment row already proves both parents existed. Implement it with a
%% single existsById on the composite key and one 404 code,
%% ENROLLMENT_NOT_FOUND. It is listed here so the grouping stays readable, not
%% because two calls are required.

use-cases/use-cases.mmd

%% Use Case Diagram — Student Management  (actor-lane / swimlane form)
%% Covers all 23 operations in ../../api-contract/. See ../traceability.md for
%% the operationId -> use case -> sequence mapping.
%% ---
%% HOW TO READ THIS DIAGRAM
%%   Association is expressed by CONTAINMENT, not by arrows: a use case sits
%%   inside the lane of the actor who triggers it. Each of the 23 use cases has
%%   exactly one actor, so the classic "actor --> use case" line carries no
%%   information a lane cannot carry — and 23 of those lines crossing the lanes
%%   is what made the previous version unreadable.
%% ---
%%   Colour carries the second dimension: WHICH APPLICATION MODULE owns the use
%%   case, i.e. which module's controller handles it.
%%     blue   = module student      green = module book
%%     purple = module course       amber = module enrollment
%%   Every use case has exactly one owning module, and it is the module whose
%%   table the operation writes to. See ../modules/module-map.mmd.
%% ---
%%   «include» relationships live in their own view: use-cases-includes.mmd.
%%   Mixing them in here is the other half of what caused the arrow overlap.

%%{init: {"flowchart": {"rankSpacing": 22, "nodeSpacing": 22, "padding": 8}}}%%
flowchart TB

  %% ===========================================================================
  %% Lane 1 — Academic Admin  (writes to student, course and enrollment)
  %% ===========================================================================
  subgraph LaneA["👤 Academic Admin — commands"]
    direction TB

    subgraph A_student["Student lifecycle"]
      direction TB
      UC1([UC1 · Create Student])
      UC4([UC4 · Update Student])
      UC5([UC5 · Delete Student])
    end

    subgraph A_course["Course lifecycle"]
      direction TB
      UC6([UC6 · Create Course])
      UC9([UC9 · Update Course])
      UC10([UC10 · Delete Course])
    end

    subgraph A_enrol["Enrollment"]
      direction TB
      UC11([UC11 · Enroll Student in Course])
      UC12([UC12 · Unenroll Student from Course])
    end
  end

  %% ===========================================================================
  %% Lane 2 — Library Admin  (writes to the book module only)
  %% ===========================================================================
  subgraph LaneL["👤 Library Admin — commands"]
    direction TB

    subgraph L_book["Book lifecycle"]
      direction TB
      UC15([UC15 · Create Book])
      UC18([UC18 · Update Book])
      UC19([UC19 · Delete Book])
    end

    subgraph L_own["Ownership"]
      direction TB
      UC20([UC20 · Assign Book to Student])
      UC21([UC21 · Unassign Book from Student])
    end
  end

  %% ===========================================================================
  %% Lane 3 — API Client  (reads only; spans both modules)
  %% ===========================================================================
  subgraph LaneC["🖥️ API Client — queries"]
    direction TB

    subgraph C_acad["Student · Course · Enrollment reads"]
      direction TB
      UC2([UC2 · Get Student by ID])
      UC3([UC3 · List Students])
      UC7([UC7 · Get Course by ID])
      UC8([UC8 · List Courses])
      UC13([UC13 · List Courses of a Student])
      UC14([UC14 · List Students in a Course])
    end

    subgraph C_lib["Book reads"]
      direction TB
      UC16([UC16 · Get Book by ID])
      UC17([UC17 · List Books])
      UC22([UC22 · List Books Owned by a Student])
      UC23([UC23 · Get Owner of a Book])
    end
  end

  %% ===========================================================================
  %% Legend
  %% ===========================================================================
  subgraph Legend["Legend — colour = owning application module"]
    direction TB
    LG1([module: student])
    LG2([module: course])
    LG3([module: book])
    LG4([module: enrollment])
    LG5([lane = the actor who triggers the use case])
  end

  %% ===========================================================================
  %% Layout only — invisible links (~~~) carry NO meaning.
  %% Without them a diagram with no real edges collapses into one flat row:
  %% every node lands on rank 0. One chain per lane stacks that lane's groups
  %% top-to-bottom and lets the three lanes sit side by side.
  %% ===========================================================================
  UC1 ~~~ UC4 ~~~ UC5 ~~~ UC6 ~~~ UC9 ~~~ UC10 ~~~ UC11 ~~~ UC12
  UC15 ~~~ UC18 ~~~ UC19 ~~~ UC20 ~~~ UC21
  UC2 ~~~ UC3 ~~~ UC7 ~~~ UC8 ~~~ UC13 ~~~ UC14 ~~~ UC16 ~~~ UC17 ~~~ UC22 ~~~ UC23
  LG1 ~~~ LG2 ~~~ LG3 ~~~ LG4 ~~~ LG5

  classDef mStudent fill:#e8ecff,stroke:#3b4a9c,color:#111;
  classDef mCourse fill:#efe8ff,stroke:#6b4a9c,color:#111;
  classDef mBook fill:#e6f6ea,stroke:#2f7d46,color:#111;
  classDef mEnrol fill:#fff4e0,stroke:#b8860b,color:#111;
  classDef note fill:#fff,stroke:#bbb,color:#555,stroke-dasharray:3 3;

  class UC1,UC2,UC3,UC4,UC5,LG1 mStudent
  class UC6,UC7,UC8,UC9,UC10,LG2 mCourse
  class UC15,UC16,UC17,UC18,UC19,UC20,UC21,UC22,UC23,LG3 mBook
  class UC11,UC12,UC13,UC14,LG4 mEnrol
  class LG5 note

  style LaneA fill:#fffdf5,stroke:#c9a227,stroke-width:2px
  style LaneL fill:#fffdf5,stroke:#c9a227,stroke-width:2px
  style LaneC fill:#fffdf5,stroke:#c9a227,stroke-width:2px
  style Legend fill:#fafafa,stroke:#ddd

%% =============================================================================
%% Actor coverage — 8 + 5 + 10 = 23, a clean partition (no use case has two actors)
%% =============================================================================
%% Academic Admin  UC1  UC4  UC5  UC6  UC9  UC10 UC11 UC12
%% Library Admin   UC15 UC18 UC19 UC20 UC21
%% API Client      UC2  UC3  UC7  UC8  UC13 UC14 UC16 UC17 UC22 UC23
%% ---
%% =============================================================================
%% Module coverage — 5 + 5 + 9 + 4 = 23
%% =============================================================================
%% student     UC1  UC2  UC3  UC4  UC5
%% course      UC6  UC7  UC8  UC9  UC10
%% book        UC15 UC16 UC17 UC18 UC19 UC20 UC21 UC22 UC23
%% enrollment  UC11 UC12 UC13 UC14
%% ---
%% Two groupings that surprise people, and why they are right:
%%   UC22 "List Books Owned by a Student" is a BOOK use case even though its URL
%%     starts /students/{id}/books. Ownership is a column on books, so the book
%%     module answers it — StudentBookController lives in book/.
%%   UC14 "List Students in a Course" is an ENROLLMENT use case even though its
%%     URL starts /courses/{id}. The roster is the set of enrollment rows; the
%%     course module has no idea who is enrolled.
%% ---
%% The rule behind both: a use case belongs to the module that owns the TABLE it
%% reads or writes, not to the module named first in its URL.
%% ---
%% =============================================================================
%% Business rules attached to use cases  (see ../classes/class-diagram.mmd)
%% =============================================================================
%% UC1  Create Student   409 if studentCode or email already exists
%% UC4  Update Student   409 if the new studentCode/email belongs to another student
%% UC5  Delete Student   publishes StudentDeleted -> the book module releases
%%                       owned books and the enrollment module drops enrollments
%%                       -> then the student row is removed. All in one
%%                       transaction. Books and Courses survive.
%% UC6  Create Course    409 if courseCode already exists; credits must be positive
%% UC10 Delete Course    publishes CourseDeleted -> the enrollment module drops
%%                       the course's enrollments -> then the course row is
%%                       removed. Students survive.
%% UC11 Enroll           409 if (studentId, courseId) already enrolled
%% UC15 Create Book      409 if isbn already exists
%% UC19 Delete Book      ownership disappears with the book. No event is
%%                       published — nothing references a book. The owner survives.
%% UC20 Assign Book      409 if the book is already owned by a different student
%% UC21 Unassign Book    404 if the book is not owned by that student.
%%                       Clears ownerId only — the book is NOT deleted.
%% UC23 Get Book Owner   404 if the book exists but has no owner
%% ---
%% UC3, UC8, UC17 support page / size / sort / search per
%% ../../api-contract/components/parameters/.
%% ---
%% =============================================================================
%% Caveat on actors
%% =============================================================================
%% The Academic Admin / Library Admin / API Client split is ASPIRATIONAL. The
%% current OpenAPI contract defines no security scheme and spring-boot-starter-
%% security is commented out in management/pom.xml, so every operation is in
%% practice reachable by any caller. The split documents intended authority for
%% a future authorization story; it is not an implementable requirement today.
